stories.title: Tatum scores 41 to help Celtics snap 4-game skid with a 131-116 win over Wizards
stories.summary: — Jayson Tatum scored 28 of his 41 points in the first half and the Boston Celtics snapped their four-game losing streak by beating the Washington Wizards 131-116 on Tuesday night.
stories.detailText: WASHINGTON -- — Jayson Tatum scored 28 of his 41 points in the first half and the Boston Celtics snapped their four-game losing streak by beating the Washington Wizards 131-116 on Tuesday night. The Celtics made 10 3-pointers during a 46-point second quarter. That gave Boston an 80-49 lead at halftime, and although Washington cut the deficit to five with a spirited second-half effort, the Celtics held on. The Celtics remained unbeaten in NBA Cup play, and Washington is mathematically eliminated. Paul George scored 28 points for Boston, and Neemias Queta had 21. Anthony Davis had 33 points and 13 rebounds for the Wizards. Kyshawn George added 24 points and rookie AJ Dybantsa had 20 points, 11 rebounds and seven assists. Trae Young scored 17 points with 12 assists. Queta scored 13 points for Boston before Davis, the opposing big man, managed any. That helped the Celtics to a 34-28 lead after one quarter, and then the bottom fell out for the Wizards. Boston began the second quarter with a 14-3 run, and the Celtics later went on an 11-0 streak — with three 3-pointers by Tatum — to lead 70-38. Boston faces Atlanta on Friday night, with the winner finishing atop this NBA Cup group. Washington had a three-game winning streak snapped. The Wizards haven't won four in a row since a six-game run in January 2023. Paul George left Kyshawn George on the ground with a crossover dribble, paused for effect, and sank a jumper in the third quarter. But by then the Wizards had already begun to fight back. Washington got the deficit down to 13 before the period ended. It was 117-112 after Dybantsa's bank shot, but then Tatum got free for a layup and Boston's Baylor Scheierman sank a 3 for his first points of the game. Up next Celtics: Host Atlanta on Friday night. Wizards: Host Orlando on Saturday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

stories.title: Vintage Paul George drops Kyshawn George to the floor with ankle-breaking crossover in NBA Cup play
stories.summary: Paul George is in the midst of a career renaissance in his first season with the Boston Celtics. Kyshawn George learned the hard way Tuesday night.
stories.detailText: Paul George is in the midst of a career renaissance in his first season with the Boston Celtics. Washington Wizards guard Kyshawn George learned the hard way Tuesday night. With the Celtics in control of their NBA Cup matchup in Washington, Paul sized up Kyshawn in isolation. He gained some separation with an arm extension on the perimeter, then crossed Kyshawn over as he drove to his right. Kyshawn did not stay with him. pic.twitter.com/7b33YgpVeG — Celtics Clips (@celticsclipss) November 25, 2026 Instead, Kyshawn fell on his backside on to the court and into the legs of his teammate, Anthony Davis. Paul picked up his dribble and waited a beat while shooting a glance at Kyshawn — just to make sure Kyshawn was watching. Only then did Paul pull up for a jumper from just inside the 3-point arc that sank through the net to extend Boston’s lead to 90-65. George, 36, entered Tuesday’s game doing an admirable job of making Celtics fans forget about Jaylen Brown, whom he was traded for. He’s the clear No. 2 option behind Jayson Tatum with averages of 19.9 points, 5.6 rebounds, 3.8 assists and 2.2 steals per game. He remains one of the game’s best shooters with a 40.7% success rate from 3. And as Kyshawn learned Tuesday night, Paul George has still got some moves.

stories.title: Without Cade Cunningham, Pistons get 21 from Isaiah Joe to hand Magic their first NBA Cup loss
stories.summary: — Isaiah Joe had 21 points and Daniss Jenkins added 15 to spur the Detroit Pistons past the Orlando Magic 104-86 in an NBA Cup game on Tuesday night.
stories.detailText: ORLANDO, Fla. -- — Isaiah Joe had 21 points and Daniss Jenkins added 15 to spur the Detroit Pistons past the Orlando Magic 104-86 in an NBA Cup game on Tuesday night. With leading scorer Cade Cunningham out with a knee injury, Detroit also got 13 points from Ron Holland and improved to 2-1 in NBA Cup group play. The Pistons handed Orlando its first loss of the in-season tournament, preventing the Magic from clinching East Group A. Desmond Bane had 21 and Franz Wagner scored 20 for Orlando, which now must wait for Detroit, Brooklyn, Milwaukee and Toronto to finish the group stage before learning whether it has advanced to the knockout round. Joe, making his first start in a Pistons uniform after four seasons in Oklahoma City, scored 14 points in the second half. He made three consecutive 3-pointers in the fourth quarter to put the game out of reach. The Pistons built an 18-point lead in the third quarter and kept a healthy advantage throughout the second half. Detroit scored the game’s first eight points and, after allowing Orlando back in the game, took command in the second quarter. The Pistons used an 18-0 run to outscore Orlando 32-14 in the period and held Wagner to just two first-half points. Detroit’s Ausar Thompson had just six points but contributed 10 rebounds, seven assists and four blocks. He was key in limiting the Magic to a season-low in points. The Pistons have held opponents under 100 on six occasions, going undefeated in those games. The Pistons also outscored Orlando 19-9 on fast-break points. stories.title: Stephen A. Smith says Black NBA players have thanked him over white Lakers comments
stories.summary: Stephen A. Smith raised some eyebrows last Wednesday when he called out the NBA for potentially letting the Lakers win a championship. A team that’s led by a trio of...
stories.detailText: Stephen A. Smith raised some eyebrows last Wednesday when he called out the NBA for potentially letting the Lakers win a championship. A team that’s led by a trio of white stars in Luka Dončić, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler. The talk show personality faced a lot of scrutiny and criticism for his comments. He questioned Black NBA players for letting a group of “white brothers” “win a championship.” Stephen A. Smith reveals Black NBA players have shared their support about his white player Lakers comments. ZUMAPRESS.com But even with the scrutiny, he’s also received support. The television personality revealed on his show, “Straight Shooter,” on Tuesday night that Black NBA players have reached out to him to thank him for his comments about the Lakers trio. “You know how many brothers in the NBA reached out to me and thanked me for saying it?” Smith said. When the Lakers trio was finished being assembled in July when Los Angeles acquired Kessler via a sign-and-trade deal with the Jazz, Smith questioned the team’s decision to form the trio and said, “Your three best players are white dudes. This ain’t golf. And we got a whole bunch of brothers on Team USA. This is basketball, what y’all think this is?” Stephen A. Smith says Black NBA players have been reaching out to him and thanking him for his takes on the Lakers’ white trio (h/t @TheNBABase ) pic.twitter.com/qYR3JuEGvG — NBACentral (@TheDunkCentral) November 24, 2026 Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves standing next to each other during an NBA game. NBAE via Getty Images The Lakers entered Tuesday night tied for the NBA’s best record with the Spurs (15-3) and have been led by Dončić, who’s an early MVP candidate. Smith expressed his admiration for the trio by calling Dončić a “superstar,” Reaves “a baller,” and Kessler “no scrub,” but he doubled down on his comments and said, “The Lakers got a chance. I get it. Do I expect them to win? No.” Lakers center Walker Kessler with the ball in his hands during an NBA game. NBAE via Getty Images “I’m just saying to you. When I think of cats in the Eastern Conference and the Western Conference. If those are the three players you are riding with, when it really counts, I don’t think you’re winning a best-of-seven series and [you’re] winning a [championship],” Smith said. “I don’t think it’s happening.” While Smith doesn’t believe the Lakers stand a chance to win an NBA title, former Celtics champion Kevin Garnett called out Smith on an episode of the “KG and Stephen A.” show and said, “They making you look crazy. You talking all that s–t about them white boys, saying they can’t win, and s–t.”

stories.title: NBA Cup 2026: Celtics avert disaster behind Jayson Tatum's 41, Pistons deny Magic without Cade Cunningham
stories.summary: Boston nearly blew a 31-point halftime lead, but held on down the stretch against the Wizards.
stories.detailText: The Boston Celtics entered halftime of Tuesday’s NBA Cup game apparently well on their way to snapping a four-game losing streak . They eventually got there. But it wasn’t easy as they had to fend off a furious comeback effort from the Washington Wizards. The Celtics opened an 80-49 lead at halftime that the Wizards cut to 117-112 in the final four minutes. But the Celtics held on from there to avert disaster via a 131-116 victory. A Jayson Tatum 3 and two more by Baylor Scheierman in the game’s final minutes helped ensure that the Celtics got back into the win column. pic.twitter.com/HMOcWN193T — Celtics Clips (@celticsclipss) November 25, 2026 With the win, the Celtics improved to 3-0 in NBA Cup play to maintain control of East Group C. The Wizards dropped to 2-2 in the NBA Cup. Tatum led the effort with 41 points, 8 assists and 6 rebounds. He shot 6 of 15 from 3, but made all of them before halftime as cold second-half 3-point shooting helped the Wizards mount their rally. Boston was red-hot in the first half while shooting 15 of 26 (57.7%) from long distance. They shot 7 of 25 (28%) after halftime and needed three of those in the final minutes after the Wizards cut their deficit to five points. Ultimately, their 43.1% success rate from 3 was a cornerstone of their win, but questions will surely surface about the wisdom of continuing to hoist up 3s after building a 31-point lead. Paul George had no such struggles with a 28-point, 9-assist effort in which he shot 6 of 9 from 3. Anthony Davis led the Wizards with 33 points, 13 rebounds, 2 blocks and 1 steal. Cade Cunningham was a late scratch and watched Tuesday's Pistons win in street clothes. Rich Storry via Getty Images Pistons roll after concerning late scratch of Cade Cunningham The Detroit Pistons secured an NBA Cup win over the Orlando Magic Tuesday night, but it was overshadowed by concern for Cade Cunningham, who was a late scratch due to a lingering knee injury . The Pistons played without their All-NBA guard and cruised to a 104-86 win to hand the Magic their first loss in NBA Cup play. The Pistons (11-6) are now 2-1 in Cup play, while the Magic (7-10) drop to 3-1. The loss blocked the Magic from from a chance to clinch East Group A. Is Cunningham OK? Cunningham was listed as probable prior to the game due to lingering knee soreness. But he was a late scratch before an NBA Cup game, raising concern that his injury is one that could further linger. Head coach J.B. Bickerstaff declined to offer details on Cunningham's condition in his pregame news conference. He also didn't say much to tamp down concern. "He's battling through a lot, and I'll leave it at that," Bickerstaff said . "He's going to go out and compete and give us what he's got. But he's fighting through a lot." Cunningham had previously missed one game this season, last Wednesday's 122-109 win over the New Orleans Pelicans . He struggled in his previous outing with a season-low five points in Sunday's 107-97 loss to the Atlanta Hawks. Pistons thrive without their leader Detroit struggled to get its offense going early without Cunningham as the Magic jumped out to a 22-16 first-quarter lead on their home court. But the Pistons seized control with a 32-14 advantage in the second quarter and kept the Magic at bay from there. Isaiah Joe took Cunningham's place in the starting lineup and finished the game with a team-high 21 points alongside 4 rebounds and 1 steal. Daniss Jenkins was the primary playmaker in Cunningham's absence with 15 points and 10 assists. Desmond Bane led the Magic with 21 points and 5 assists. Detroit will next face the Milwaukee Bucks at home on Friday. The Magic will visit the Washington Wizards on Saturday. stories.title: Knicks’ fading NBA Cup hopes on line against Cavaliers
stories.summary: The Knicks’ slim NBA Cup hopes hang in the balance.
stories.detailText: Jalen Brunson, left, and Mikal Bridges of the New York Knicks high five during a game against the Indiana Pacers in New York, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. The Knicks’ slim NBA Cup hopes hang in the balance. Wednesday’s game against the Cavs at Madison Square Garden is the Knicks’ third of four group-stage games, having dropped their first two group-stage games to the 76ers and Pacers, respectively. In the three-year history of the Cup, no team has ever advanced to the knockout round with anything worse than a 3-1 record. The winner of each of the six groups along with two wild cards (the top team from each conference that finished second in its group) advances to the next round. Jalen Brunson (left) and Mikal Bridges high five during the Knicks’ win over the Pacers on Nov. 22, 2026 at Madison Square Garden. NBAE via Getty Images So while those first two losses didn’t officially eliminate the Knicks, they put them in a deep hole to defend their NBA Cup title . The Knicks enter Wednesday’s game last in their group and as the only one without a win. Another loss Wednesday would officially eliminate the Knicks. Wednesday’s matchup is already the third meeting between the Knicks and Cavs this year, having split the first two. The Knicks lost the most recent matchup 115-107 on Nov. 11 at MSG. “They were real physical in Game 2,” coach Mike Brown said after practice Tuesday. “You give them credit. They talked about keeping us off the glass and some other things and they did it. They’re a great coached team with Kenny Atkinson and a great team in general. “There’s gonna have to be a lot of things that we do better in this game, starting with the level of physicality, while getting out in transition, if we expect to get a win.” CHECK OUT THE LATEST NBA STANDINGS AND KNICKS STATS The Knicks will still be short-handed despite a two-day gap in between games. OG Anunoby (left calf strain) and Jordan Clarkson (right plantar fasciitis) are both out for Wednesday. They both missed the Knicks’ back-to-back wins Saturday and Sunday and neither practiced Tuesday. Anunoby’s injury changed from calf soreness to a calf strain, but the Knicks are still optimistic that he and Clarkson should be short-term absences and consider the duo day to day. Josh Hart (right shoulder sprain), Karl-Anthony Towns (right knee inflammation) and Miles McBride (left adductor tightness) are all questionable. All three practiced Tuesday, though. McBride was a late scratch for Sunday’s win over the Pacers due to the injury. The Cavs will be without Evan Mobley, who has a toe injury.

stories.title: Nets searching for answers as early defensive collapses fuel losing streak
stories.summary: The Brooklyn Nets have dropped five straight games, allowing a league-worst 72.2 points per first half during their NBA-long losing streak.
stories.detailText: Brooklyn Nets head coach Jordi Fernandez argues a call against the Orlando Magic at Barclays Center in New York, Friday, Nov. 20, 2026. MINNEAPOLIS — The Nets will drag the NBA’s longest losing skid into Milwaukee on Wednesday, a five-game slump, and pretty much all five losses have looked the same. Embarrass themselves defensively in the first half. Give themselves no chance to win in the second. Scratch their heads looking for answers in the postgame. Wash, rinse, repeat. Head coach Jordi Fernandez argues a call during the Nets’ loss to the Magic in an NBA Cup game on Nov. 20, 2026 at Barclays Center. Getty Images “That’s happened already too many times, where we allow teams [to get on a roll early]. It’s the best players in the world. If you allow one to go in and then everybody gets loose and makes shots, then it’s a long night,” Jordi Fernández said. When asked what the biggest problem with their defense was, Julius Randle couldn’t even pinpoint one. “We’ve got a lot. We were better earlier in the year and now we’ve got slippage in multiple areas. So we’ve gotta figure out where it is. But defense just starts with competitive nature first and then go from there,” Randle said. “It’s disappointing. But all you can do is focus on where you’re at and figure out how to get better. Figure out what’s the problem, how we can consistently compete at a high level.” The problem is, in this skid the Nets have barely competed at any level. CHECK OUT THE LATEST NBA STANDINGS AND NETS STATS They’ve allowed more than 70 points in the first half of four of the five losses, tied with Charlotte for the league’s longest slump. They’ve shown a concerning glass jaw, getting hit early and not hitting back. “Defensively, we just can’t give up 140 points. We let [Minnesota] catch their rhythm early, and that’s what happens when you give good teams rhythm early on in the game,” Mikel Brown Jr. told The Post. “We’ve got to cut that water off early, take away those wide-open shots.” In this five-game malaise, the Nets have allowed an average of 72.2 points and a 147.3 defensive rating in their first halves. They’ve conceded 55.9 percent shooting and 52.3 percent from deep and a minus-15.0 net rating. Every single one of those stats is not only dead last in the league, but the worst by a margin. That kind of porous defense in the first half makes the second half all but moot. “Yes, it’s always been for us to get off to a good start,” Brown told The Post. “I really just feel like just disrupting them early on. Anytime we disrupt the team early on in the game, we come out and we fight hard. And sometimes we pull out the win, and sometimes we don’t. “But it’s really just the early [part] in the game. You just can’t let good players get great shots early on in the games. You give those looks to those great players, they’re gonna start flowing, and then next thing you know, they shoot 50 percent, 55 percent from the field as a team. It’s a snowball effect that we just can’t have.”

stories.summary: Pistons center Jalen Duren has taken a significant step toward returning from injury, practicing with the team Tuesday.
stories.detailText: ORLANDO, Fla. -- Detroit Pistons center Jalen Duren has taken a significant step toward returning from injury, practicing with the team Tuesday, a day before beginning a rehab assignment. Duren strained his right hamstring on Oct. 23, in Detroit's second game. Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff said Duren took part in practice with the team ahead of Tuesday's game against Orlando . But the All-Star will miss his 15th straight game before heading out for a rehab assignment Wednesday with the organization's G League affiliate, the Motor City Cruise. "We know what he means to our team," Bickerstaff said, "how he can impact us in a positive way. Not only with the physical stuff, but the spirit and mental piece of it." Duren helped the Pistons to the Eastern Conference playoffs last season, averaging a career-best 19.5 points. Playing all but two games without Duren this season, Detroit is off to a 10-6 start, tied for fifth in the conference. Third-year forward Ausar Thompson has helped to fill the void left by Duren's absence and has led the team by averaging 8.6 rebounds. Guard Cade Cunningham leads the club in scoring, averaging 24.2 points. Bickerstaff said he's looking forward to Duren's return. "He's an anchor for us on both ends of the floor," he said. "With his ability to put the ball in his hands, he can create for himself and create for others."

stories.title: Game Preview #19: Wolves at Thunder Thread
stories.summary: Oklahoma City is bruised and battered, but still have to play host to Minnesota for an all-important NBA Cup game.
stories.detailText: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander getting shocked by Anthony Edwards’ electric jersey Well, if it isn’t our old friends the Oklahoma City Thunder? They’ve been suffering through their second straight year of heavy injuries, but the Wolves aren’t the shoulder to cry on. One team has managed to reshape their roster and stay afloat despite losing their best player and other rotation to various ailments, the other is barely staying afloat while dealing with their own litany of players sidelined. Let’s see what we got cooking on Thanksgiving eve. Game Info Who: Minnesota Timberwolves (13-5) at Oklahoma City Thunder (10-8) When: Wednesday, November 25 at 6:30 PM CT Where: Paycom Center — Oklahoma City, OK Local TV: ESPN Radio: 830 WCCO The Numbers Overall rating MIN OKC OFFRTG * 114.9 (11th) 114.0 (13th) OFFRTG DEFRTG * 104.4 (1st) 111.0 (8th) DEFRTG NETRTG * 10.5 (2nd) 3.0 (11th) NETRTG Four factors MIN OKC eFG% * 55.9 (4th) 52.6 (21st) eFG% FTr * .283 (13th) .239 (27th) FTr TOV% 16.1 (20th) * 12.8 (2nd) TOV% OREB% * 33.5 (10th) 31.2 (16th) OREB% Scoring profile MIN OKC 3PAr * .423 (18th) .354 (29th) 3PAr PITP * 51.7 (4th) 51.4 (5th) PITP 2nd PTS * 16.2 (12th) 15.6 (18th) 2nd PTS PACE * 100.72 (7th) 99.36 (18th) PACE FBPS * 16.9 (7th) 11.8 (23rd) FBPS Transition Freq * .197 (5th) .143 (29th) Transition Freq Isolation Freq .095 (4th) * .100 (2nd) Isolation Freq AST% *.603 (27th) .550 (30th) AST% * – Denotes leader What to Watch For The face of fear The back-to-back reigning Most Valuable Player, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, is number two league-wide in total free throws attempted. Sixth in total fouls drawn. I’m just listing that here for no particular reason. SGA is also having his least efficient scoring season since the 2021-22 campaign. His three-point shooting volume is up, but it shouldn’t be surprising to see his two-point percentage come down. It’s because he hasn’t been flanked by three of his starters: Jalen Williams suffered a gruesome leg injury, Cason Wallace tore his shoulder labrum, and Chet Holmgren has a tear in his knee. Many of these are long-term, if not season-ending, ailments. The Thunder are finally feeling fear for the first time in the regular season in a while. Shai has been forced to carry his team more than he’s ever had to. His .358 usage percentage is second in the league behind just Luka Dončić. He’s felt it, quite literally. He had to miss a game on Sunday due to a neck/back issue. Will he be at 100% against the Wolves on Wednesday? The Thunder better hope so. Thunder newbies Oklahoma City has long been known for their incredible depth (and collection of future draft picks). In fact, they were so rich in depth that they were paying to get off of rotation role players like Lu Dort, Isaiah Joe, and Aaron Wiggins. Had they known their starters were going to get bitten by the injury bug so badly, they’d probably undo some of those decisions. They’re currently leaning heavily on holdovers like Isaiah Hartenstein and Kenrich Williams. Until then, they’ve had some rookies and unfamiliar faces step up. You may recognize the pair of 2024 rookies in Ajay Mitchell and Jared McCain, who are the second and third leading scorers on the team. Additionally, their 2026 rookies have been a pleasant surprise for them. Mara has been force in the paint on both ends of the court, doing his best Holmgren impression. He stands at 7’2” and has a wingspan longer than Rocco Zikarsky (but shorter than Rudy’s). Meanwhile, Stirtz has come on as of late, becoming a legitimate perimeter scoring threat. Thunder general manager Sam Presti know how to pick ‘em. Minnesota should be wise to not get caught sleeping on ‘em. UPDATE : Aday Mara is ruled out for Wednesday’s game. Alex Caruso is returning from a three-game absence which will take away from Stirtz’s minutes. Shut down SGA; OKC goes away This is a very casual observation, but the Thunder currently go only as far as Shai can take them. Their turnover rate is so low because they rely so much on isolation, particularly from SGA. They literally have to hope he can muster up enough points to carry them to a slim margin of victory. In Oklahoma City’s past eight games, they’ve won just two of them. The opponents were the Sacramento Kings and New Orleans Pelicans. Shai had to score 37 or more to even defeat those bottom-feeders (respectfully). Minnesota has no shortage of defenders they can throw at him. The Thunder are a fairly small team (they just started Micah Peavy, a 6’7” guard, at power forward) so that should allow for guys Jaden McDaniels and Jonathan Kuminga to get opportunities to stop the Canadian. stories.detailText: Brandon Williams speaks about the Golden State Warriors' offensive struggles. Brandon Williams is just one of the casualties who has been affected by injuries in the Golden State Warriors’ locker room, and it’s resulted in the team struggling offensively. Williams, who is nearing a return, was asked if he sees himself as someone who will bring “some juice” to the team’s offense and admitted he hopes so. Williams also revealed that it’s been tough to watch lately. Brandon Williams and Steph Curry on the court laughing during an NBA game against the Mavericks. NBAE via Getty Images “I ain’t gonna lie, that s–t been tough watching that, but I know exactly what I need to do,” Williams said. “Just watching from afar, not being in the game, you see a little bit more.” Williams admitted the Warriors’ offense has been getting “stagnant at times” and wants to be part of fixing it. “I know that’s what they brought me in here for, to keep it rolling, keep it going, keep everybody organized,” Williams said. Williams has been out with a hamstring injury he suffered on Nov. 9 against the Pelicans. He said he noticed his hamstring started hurting during the first play of the game but wanted to see if he could continue playing. Brandon Williams is eager to return after being sidelined due to injury. NBAE via Getty Images Williams said on the second defensive possession, he wanted to “test it out” by performing a move he usually does when he was guarding Jordan Poole, and that’s when he noticed it started to tighten. “I felt it that second time with Jordan Poole, we called a timeout, and the entire timeout, I was stretching it out a little bit,” Williams said. “Then I came back here, and ultimately, it just led to me being out.” Williams is in his first season with the Warriors and has been one of their better shooters not named Steph Curry. Since his injury, he remains fourth in shooting on the team and is averaging 10.4 points per game, behind Brandin Podziemski, Yaxel Lendeborg and Curry. The fifth-year veteran signed with the Warriors during the offseason on a one-year, $2.6 million contract to be a role player after averaging 13 points with the Mavericks last season. Wednesday will mark two weeks since Golden State has been without Curry, who suffered an oblique tear against the Rockets . Last Sunday was the first time they had won a game since. Golden State Warriors forward Draymond Green celebrating during Sunday’s win against the Celtics. Getty Images Williams admitted it’s been challenging and mentally tough to deal with the team’s recent performance during its losing skid. “San Antonio game, Houston game, Pelicans, all of them,” Williams said. “Draymond [Green], Steph, Al [Horford], all of them have been keeping us together, in good spirits, so we can’t keep our heads down at all.”

stories.title: Kawhi Leonard's return from knee swelling still at least week away
stories.summary: The Raptors say Kawhi Leonard's status will be revisted in a week as he recovers from knee swelling.
stories.detailText: The wait for Kawhi Leonard 's return to play from left knee swelling will extend for at least another week. The Toronto Raptors said Tuesday that the forward "continues to progress in his recovery" and that an update will be provided in a week. Leonard has begun individual on-court workouts after treatment to address the swelling, the Raptors added. Sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Oct. 27 that Leonard was expected to miss a number of weeks due to swelling in his left knee. An MRI on the knee in September showed no structural damage, and the team has provided weekly updates regarding his status. Toronto issued a similar message Nov. 17, saying that Leonard "has progressed in his strength and conditioning program." On Nov. 10, the Raptors reported that Leonard would be out at least another week and that he was "continuing his reconditioning process." Leonard posted a message on X after news initially broke that he would be out, writing that "it's always frustrating missing time." "I came back to compete with this team and I'm focused on getting back to 100. Toronto, I've appreciated the love since I've been back. Returning soon," he wrote. The two-time Defensive Player of the Year winner returned to Toronto in the offseason, agreeing to a two-year, $115 million extension after being dealt from the LA Clippers . The trade followed up a tumultuous end to his Clippers tenure. In September, the team was found guilty by the NBA of violating salary cap rules in a case involving Leonard, who wasn't suspended but was fined $700,000. Coming back to the Raptors, where he led the franchise to its only NBA title in 2019, marked a fresh start for him. So far this season, Leonard has suited up in just two games and is averaging 19.5 points, 7.5 rebounds and 1.5 assists. The earliest he can return for the 6-11 Raptors is Dec. 1 against the Houston Rockets .

stories.title: Pistons' Cade Cunningham out for Tuesday's NBA Cup matchup vs. Magic due to right knee soreness
stories.summary: Cunningham was scratched from the lineup after being listed as probable up until a half-hour before tip-off.
stories.detailText: Detroit Pistons guard Cade Cunningham missed Tuesday's 104-86 win over the Orlando Magic in NBA Cup group play . He was a late scratch due to right knee soreness after being listed as probable on the injury report until a half-hour before tip-off. Cunningham, 25, had previously missed only one game this season for the Pistons, sitting out last week's 122-109 win over the New Orleans Pelicans , also due to right knee soreness. Javonte Green replaced Cunningham in Detroit's starting lineup for that contest, scoring 18 points with seven rebounds. "He's battling through a lot, and I'll leave it at that," Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff told reporters Tuesday , via MLive's Jacob Richman. "He's going to go out and compete and give us what he's got, but he's fighting through a lot." Cunningham scored a season-low five points in Sunday's 107-97 loss to the Atlanta Hawks, shooting 2-for-9 in 33 minutes. His 15 assists were his highest total this season, but he also committed six turnovers. The Pistons have lost two straight games and have a 10-6 record that has them tied for fifth in the Eastern Conference . In his 15 games this season, Cunningham leads the Pistons in scoring with 24.2 points per game, while averaging 8.3 assists, 5.1 rebounds and 1.3 steals. He's shooting 32% on 92 3-point attempts. Detroit was also without Duncan Robinson (left quad strain) and Jalen Duren (strained right hamstring) against the Magic. However, Duren appears to be on his way back after being assigned to the Pistons' G League affiliate for Wednesday's practice. The Pistons next play on Friday versus the Milwaukee Bucks.

stories.title: Knicks’ lack of wing depth is rearing ugly head with recent injuries
stories.summary: The emphasis in the title defense is to stay healthy, but that also comes with playing some rough rotations.
stories.detailText: SAN ANTONIO, TX - JUNE 5: Pacome Dadiet #4 of the New York Knicks and Mohamed Diawara #51 of the New York Knicks smiles before the game against the San Antonio Spurs during Game Two of the 2026 NBA Finals on June 5, 2026 at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Garrett Ellwood/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Since the mountain of injuries single-handedly derailed the Knicks’ 2024 playoff run, they’ve been the pinnacle of health around the NBA. Aside from dealing with the lack of durability from Mitchell Robinson, almost no long-term injuries have hampered the Knicks’ playoff aspirations. Even the more bothersome injuries, Landry Shamet’s shoulder issues, Deuce McBride’s core surgery, and Jalen Brunson’s nagging ankles, all resolve themselves before the postseason. Coming off a grueling championship run and attempting an exceptionally difficult repeat in an age of parity, injuries are the looming threat that could derail things before they get started. It’s no wonder, then, that the team has been playing it safe with minor ailments to Jose Alvarado and Josh Hart over the last few weeks, but two more issues have sprung up over the last few days. Jordan Clarkson is dealing with a bout of plantar fasciitis, and OG Anunoby has a calf strain. Both of these could easily be resolved in under a week, but could both also derail both of their seasons. Plantar fasciitis can be managed, which is likely what the team is trying to do, but more severe bouts that build up over time could leave players out for months. Calf injuries in recent years have been a dangerous precursor for Achilles tears, as seen with Kevin Durant and Tyrese Haliburton in recent years. Even if it’s a mild strain, it is imperative to take it slow. That might mean no Anunoby for a while, even if no timetable has been presented. For a coach like Mike Brown who loves to experiment in the regular season, that might not seem like too bad. For us fans? It means seeing some… interesting lineup combinations in close games. It’s one thing when they played around with Dalton Knecht and Mo Diawara against the Bucks and Bulls, but Pacôme Dadiet? Now that’s something. Landry Shamet seems to have replaced Anunoby in the starting lineup, and although his incredible shooting and great defense are providing a spark to a starting five that usually starts sluggish (Starters w/Shamet replacing Anunoby have a +29.4 net rating in 15 minutes, compared to -12.9 with the regulars), he lacks size. This presents a problem that the Knicks knew they had, but it has further exacerbated the team’s quietest shortcoming: wing depth. In a perfect world, Diawara would’ve taken the next step in his development and firmly entrenched himself in the rotation, but he’s been passed over for Dadiet in the last week for those bench wing minutes vacated by the injuries. Part of me thinks it’s an attempt to raise the expiring French wing’s trade value, but it could be something in practice prompting this opportunity. Since Diawara signed his four-year extension in July, there’s been no sign of improvement. He struggled in Summer League and has been fairly regular in any action he’s had since. That’s opened the door for Dadiet, who, although seems more confident from three-point range, has also been unspectacular. It’s hard to hide them in a lineup offensively given the roster construction. Sure, ideally, you have Karl-Anthony Towns or Jalen Brunson on the court at all times, but that’s just one player. When one is off the court, either Tyler Kolek or Andre Drummond is on, and neither are any threat to score. Surround that with Hart’s offensive struggles, Mikal Bridges’ inconsistency, and the limited games of McBride and Shamet, and you have some painful offensive stretches. When Brown gets more involved, it gets better, but teams don’t want to be constantly running stuff: I have the Knicks at 331 star-less half-court poss. (no KAT, no Brunson) 0.81 PPP no star, 0.98 PPP w/star BUT… 0.82 PPP / 1.02 ePPP when they run offense (63% rate, good) 0.69 PPP / 0.92 ePPP when they don't Wide action⬇️ and then Toppin still thinks he's a Knick pic.twitter.com/Kfwx8zaKSf — Shax (@ShaxNBA) November 23, 2026 The options are extremely limited, and if you try to look deeper than Diawara or Dadiet, you get two guys who shoot and don’t do much else (Tyler Nickel, Knecht). That’s it. This isn’t that big of a deal if Anunoby’s strain is mild and he’s back soon. Injuries happen, and everyone has to eventually play the end of the bench in unenviable situations over a grueling 82-game season, so Brown will just hold his nose and rely on his army of small-to-medium-sized guards in these spots and hope they won’t get burned when the better teams eventually come. But long term, could the Knicks use another warm body? The Knicks are unable to sign a 15th player until February 13, squarely in buyout market territory, and it’s far too soon to tell who could be available. There’s also the trade deadline with some interesting contract situations on the roster, but is getting an insurance policy the top priority over, say, an upgrade at backup center? We’re well past the Vince Goodwill fake panic of the first few weeks, and the Knicks are sitting pretty in a three-way tie at second in the East through 17 games, but maybe the front office will need to get to work on more than they originally thought they would have to.

stories.title: NBA Injury Update: Latest news on Tyrese Haliburton, Jalen Duren, Donte DiVincenzo
stories.summary: It's good to see some stars about to come off the injured list.
stories.detailText: In an NBA season that has seemed defined by high-profile injuries, there was a lot of good news on Nov. 24 about players nearing a return. Here is the latest. Tyrese Haliburton could return this week There may be no more optimistic news about Tyrese Haliburton's return to the Pacers than this: When normally stoic, cautious coach Rick Carlisle was asked on Indianapolis' 107.5 The Fan if Haliburton might return this week, this was his response: "Stay tuned." Earlier this week, the Pacers assigned Haliburton to their G League squad for a day to get in a full practice, a clear sign he is nearing a return. Haliburton had posted on Instagram that his goal was to return before the end of November, and the Pacers play two more games this month, a back-to-back Friday hosting the Philadelphia 76ers, then traveling on Saturday to face the Chicago Bulls. Indiana has gone 4-10 with Haliburton out due to a hamstring strain. The Pacers both don't want to push him back and need him — their offense is built around his playmaking. In the four games he played, Haliburton averaged 21.8 points and 9.5 assists per game, but that undersells how important he is to this team. Pistons’ Jalen Duren nearing return As noted in the Haliburton note, a clear sign a player is close to returning is him being assigned to the club's G-League team to get in a full practice (NBA teams rarely have those kinds of practices during the season). With that, the Detroit Pistons sent out this note Tuesday on injured center Jalen Duren: "Jalen Duren (right hamstring strain) will be assigned to the Motor City Cruise, the NBA's G League affiliate of the Detroit Pistons, tomorrow for a practice as part of his return to play." That's a good sign. The Pistons also noted that Duncan Robinson is now day-to-day recovering from a quad strain. Donte DiVincenzo reportedly targeting January return Donte DiVincenzo has been out since tearing his right Achilles tendon during the first round of the playoffs last April. Now, he "has been cleared for team basketball activities and is progressing toward his return to play," the team announced Tuesday. There is no timeline attached, but the well-connected Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic reports he is targeting a January return, nine months after the injury. Other injury news • Denver's Julian Strawther, who sprained his knee in the preseason and has been out ever since, is off the injury report and could play as early as Tuesday against Dallas. • Charlotte sharpshooter Kon Knueppel is "weeks away" from playing due to the hamstring strain that has kept him out all season, reports Rod Boone of The Boone Docs . • If you missed the bad news from Monday, the Grizzlies star rookie Cameron Boozer is out at least a month with a hamstring strain . Also, the best player from the Nets' 2005 draft class, Nolan Traore, will be out 8-10 weeks with a hamstring strain.

stories.title: Joel Embiid doubtful for Sixers’ NBA Cup showdown vs. Miami Heat
stories.summary: Joel Embiid’s illness clearly does not respect the Cup. Sad!
stories.detailText: MIAMI, FLORIDA - MARCH 30: Bam Adebayo #13 of the Miami Heat and Joel Embiid #21 of the Philadelphia 76ers talk during a free throw in thew fourth quarter of a game at Kaseya Center on March 30, 2026 in Miami, Florida. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Sixers are getting dangerously close to full strength, which means in true Sixers fashion, calamity is right around the corner. Lo and behold, Joel Embiid came down with an illness that caused him to miss Monday’s game against the Portland Trail Blazers, and he’s still dealing with it a day later. Embiid is doubtful to suit up for the Sixers’ NBA Cup game against the Miami Heat on Wednesday, according to the NBA’s injury report . The good news is that aside from Embiid and Ariel Hukporti (Achilles), no one else is even listed for the Sixers. So much for Jaylen Brown’s hamstring injury! On Miami’s side, two-way signees Tre Donaldson and Vladislav Goldin are out on assignment in the G League, while Myron Gardner is available. The big question mark is Giannis Antetokounmpo, who’s listed as questionable with right groin tendinitis. He missed Miami’s win over the Oklahoma City Thunder on Sunday with the same injury, and in his absence, Bam Adebayo messed around and got a triple-double. If Giannis is able to suit up and Embiid misses the game, the Sixers will have a hell of a time stopping him and Bam down low. None of Jabari Walker, Dominick Barlow or Adem Bona have the size to combat the Greek Freak in transition. But if Giannis does sit out, it’ll be more of a fair fight. The Heat sit atop East Group B with a 2-0 record, while the Sixers are 1-1. If the Heat beat the Sixers, they’ll be all but guaranteed to win the group, as they’ll have the head-to-head tiebreaker over both the Sixers and Cleveland Cavaliers. But if the Embiid-less Sixers can take down the Heat, they’ll have a chance to win Group B as long as the New York Knicks beat the Cavs later Wednesday. The Sixers have never advanced to the knockout stage of the NBA Cup, but they’ve also never had NBA Cup MVP LeBron James on their roster before this year. And since LeBron is playing on a veteran-minimum contract this year, the prize money for winning the Cup would be more than 10 percent of his salary. That’s assuredly a huge motivation for someone with an estimated net worth of $1.4 billion . Embiid’s likely absence will give the Sixers a chance to continue experimenting with their backup options as they inch closer to the start of unofficial trade season. They largely went with a Walker-Barlow combo against the Blazers—Bona played only five minutes in his first game back from a cervical spine sprain—but it’s worth keeping an eye on whether the Sixers change that up against the Heat. They should still be in the intel-gathering stage of the season, so the more they mix it up, the better. (Could we even get some brief Tacko Time?) As someone whose two-year-old is just getting over hand, foot and mouth disease, it’s that time of the year for parents. Here’s hoping the rest of the Sixers stay healthy and Embiid feels better soon.

stories.title: LeBron Log No. 6: A Rocky night, a shooting lesson and a fight over ‘Bron'
stories.summary: James took the Sixers to see "I Play Rocky," knocked down threes against Portland and sued the makers of a betting research app.
stories.detailText: LeBron Log No. 6: A Rocky night, a shooting lesson and a fight over ‘Bron' originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia It was another eventful week for LeBron James. When is it not? That’s why we started the LeBron Log in the first place. The King spent his latest week taking his teammates to the movies, fighting over his name in federal court and producing his best three-point shooting performance as a Sixer days after recording a podcast about the craft. This week also marks 20 years since James faced the Sixers alongside Allen Iverson. Welcome to the sixth edition. WE WATCH ROCKY James found an appropriate choice for the Sixers’ latest team outing. He organized a private screening of I Play Rocky on Friday night for players, their families and members of the basketball operations staff. The film follows Sylvester Stallone’s fight to get the original Rocky made while insisting that he play the title character. “I mean, it’s Rocky. We in Philly,” James said. “I heard it was a great movie, and we had a night off. I’ve got a few connections, and I was able to bring that to my teammates and this organization for us to watch it. I thought it was a great movie. Unbelievably cast. Everyone looked like exactly who they were portraying. That is Hollywood for you. It was pretty cool.” The Sixers shared photos of James alongside Jaylen Brown, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Labaron Philon Jr., Jabari Walker, Tacko Fall and Adem Bona. “Movie night, courtesy of LeBron,” the team wrote. View this post on Instagram The nationwide release of I Play Rocky came less than two weeks before Philadelphia celebrates the 50th anniversary of the original film on Dec. 3. Nick Nurse could not attend because of a previous commitment, but he received positive reviews from his players. “They went, they said it was very good, they loved it,” Nurse said. “The big takeaway was how much Anthony actually looked like Rocky. Or Sylvester Stallone. One in the same.” James’ first season in Philadelphia now includes a private Rocky screening. A trip up the Art Museum steps remains available for a future edition. FROM THE PODCAST TO THE BUZZER James and Steve Nash devoted the latest episode of their Mind the Game podcast to the art of shooting. The two examined shooting form, confidence, repetitions, free throws and some of their favorite jumpers. James also revealed one detail that can affect what he does after catching the ball. “I’m a guy who don’t like shooting against the laces,” James said. “So sometimes I’ll come up on a quick stop and I’m about to raise and I can feel the laces not fixed. I’ll turn that into a pump fake.” The episode was released Nov. 17, while James was experiencing an extended struggle from three-point range. It did not provide an instant fix. James went 1 for 5 from three against Orlando and missed his lone attempt against Milwaukee. He entered Monday night’s meeting with Portland shooting 21.7 percent from deep through his first 13 games. Then he caught fire. James made all three of his first-half attempts from three. He ended the second quarter by pump-faking, stepping to his left and beating the buzzer with a corner three that tied the game at 69. Nobody could see where the laces sat on the catch. The pump fake was clear. James finished 4 for 5 from three and scored a season-high 23 points on 8-for-13 shooting. It was his third consecutive game with at least 20 points, following 22 against Orlando and 21 against Milwaukee. The Sixers lost to Portland, 128-111, but James produced his best long-range performance since joining them. Six days after discussing the art of shooting, he provided a brief demonstration. A FIGHT OVER ‘BRON’ James is also attempting to protect one of his most recognizable nicknames. James and LBJ Trademarks LLC filed a federal lawsuit on Nov. 17 against PlayVision Inc. and its founders over a sports-betting research app initially called “Bron.” The complaint alleges that the company used an AI-generated version of James in an advertisement without his permission. The figure wore a No. 23 jersey with “Bron” across the back and resembled James through its voice, build and tattoos. It also scrolled through wagers involving NBA players. The lawsuit alleges that the advertisement falsely created the impression that James endorsed the app and suggested that he considered betting on NBA games. The complaint said the video received roughly 1 million views before it was removed. “The integrity of NBA competition, and the public’s confidence that players are not betting on the games they play, is of paramount importance to the league, its players and its fans,” the complaint said. “Any suggestion that an active NBA player is betting on NBA games is therefore far from a trivial matter, and it should not be used for clicks and views.” The app offered odds comparisons, betting trends and tracking tools but did not directly accept wagers, according to its developer. PlayVision renamed it “Evie” on Nov. 18, one day after James filed the lawsuit. James is seeking an injunction and unspecified damages. The case remains active in the Southern District of New York. CLEVELAND – NOVEMBER 25: LeBron James #23 of the Cleveland Cavaliers looks to pass off when double teamed by the Philadelphia 76ers November 25, 2006 at The Quicken Loans Arena in Cleveland, Ohio. Copyright 2006 NBAE (Photo by David Liam Kyle/NBAE via Getty Images) TWENTY YEARS LATER James spent Thanksgiving weekend in 2006 on the other side of the Sixers-Cavaliers matchup. On Nov. 25, 2006, a 21-year-old James recorded 25 points, 11 assists, four rebounds and one block in Cleveland’s 108-95 win over Philadelphia. Donning the Cavs’ old-school orange threads, he played nearly 41 minutes. Iverson led the Sixers with 31 points. Andre Iguodala added 17 points and eight rebounds, while Kyle Korver made three three-pointers off the bench. James recorded 11 assists that night. Nearly 20 years later, another 11-assist performance against Indiana moved him past Jason Kidd for third place in NBA history. The 2006 meeting also came near the end of Iverson’s original run with Philadelphia. The Sixers traded him to Denver less than a month later. James was 21. Iverson was nearing his departure. Twenty years later, James is wearing a Sixers uniform and Iverson’s No. 3 hangs above his home floor.

stories.title: Sixers' record-setting wait for the West ends against Trail Blazers
stories.summary: Philadelphia will face their first Western Conference opponent in Game 18 against a 10-6 Portland team with several familiar faces.
stories.detailText: Sixers' record-setting wait for the West ends against Trail Blazers originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia Have you noticed anything different about the Sixers’ season? No, not the fact that LeBron James and Jaylen Brown are wearing red, white and blue and have helped Philadelphia build an Eastern Conference-leading 14-3 record. The difference is hidden in their schedule. All 17 games have come against Eastern Conference opponents. When the Sixers welcome the Portland Trail Blazers to Xfinity Mobile Arena on Monday night, it will mark the latest they have ever gone into a season before facing a Western Conference team. Philadelphia’s 18-game wait also ties the 1979-80 Atlanta Hawks for the second latest by an Eastern Conference team. Only the 1980-81 Milwaukee Bucks went longer, meeting the West for the first time in their 21st game. The other side of the standings The Sixers have played who has been placed in front of them and won five consecutive games. They have already beaten the Knicks twice and own victories over Cleveland and Detroit. Their first Western Conference matchup introduces a different comparison. The West entered Monday with 11 teams above .500. The East had seven. Western Conference teams were also 41-20 against the East through Sunday. Portland will not answer every question about how the Sixers compare with the other conference. It begins a more varied portion of their schedule. The Sixers will face Memphis and Denver on consecutive nights next week. Dallas and Houston visit later in December before Philadelphia travels to play the Lakers, Clippers, Kings and Suns over a six-day stretch. Portland presents a difficult first look Portland is 10-6 under first-year head coach Micah Nori, the father of Phillies prospect Dante Nori. The Blazers are averaging 116.1 points while allowing 110.3 per game, with both figures ranking in the top 10. Their 15.4 made three-pointers per game rank second in the NBA. Deni Avdija leads Portland with 23.9 points per game. Damian Lillard is averaging 20.6 points in his return to the franchise, while 7-foot-2 center Donovan Clingan has supplied size around a deep group of guards and wings. Clingan posted 22 points and 13 rebounds Saturday night at Madison Square Garden. Portland erased a 26-point deficit and briefly took the lead before Mikal Bridges made a game-winning three-pointer at the buzzer. The 97-96 loss dropped the Blazers to 1-3 over their last four games. Slow starts have followed them during that stretch. “Our last three games, we haven’t gotten off to great starts, and that’s just something that we got to correct,” Lillard said . “Our energy and our focus and our intent has to be better from the jump. We can’t let this trend continue.” The Sixers know something about overcoming early deficits. Six of their 14 victories have required double-digit comebacks. Portland will be missing two major pieces. Ja Morant is out with a left hamstring strain, while Shaedon Sharpe remains sidelined following right meniscus surgery. Even without Morant, the Blazers can turn to Lillard, Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson to initiate their offense. Avdija and Toumani Camara provide size on the perimeter, while Clingan gives Portland the kind of interior presence that has occasionally troubled the Sixers. A reunion for Simons and Walker Anfernee Simons and Jabari Walker know the Portland organization better than any other Sixers. The two shared the floor for 128 games with the Trail Blazers . Portland won 43 of them. Their responsibilities have changed in Philadelphia. So have the expectations. Simons scored 18 points in each of the Sixers’ last two games and made seven three-pointers. He started in place of Tyrese Maxey against Orlando and hit the clinching three in his hometown. Three nights later, he supplied four more threes off the bench in the Sixers’ 132-129 win over Milwaukee . Walker has also found steady work during the Sixers’ recent frontcourt injuries. He recorded nine points, seven rebounds and four assists against the Bucks after scoring 11 against Indiana and hitting a go-ahead three late in Orlando. Both players recently discussed how their difficult seasons in Portland changed their perspective on filling smaller roles for a winning team. “You feel appreciative of the times where you go into a situation where your role might be a little bit less, but you’re winning,” Simons said. “That’s something that you can’t take for granted, for sure, because it’s hard to win in the NBA. We’ve seen it firsthand.” Their former team will now see them operating within a deeper rotation than the one Philadelphia carried through much of the past week. Reinforcements could be coming Brown, Dean Wade and Adem Bona were all listed as probable on the Sixers’ initial injury report after missing time. Brown and Wade have each missed the last two games. Bona has been sidelined since Nov. 4 because of a cervical spine sprain. Dominick Barlow returned Saturday and scored 12 points on 5-for-6 shooting in his season debut. Joel Embiid was added to the injury report Monday morning as questionable because of an illness. His availability will determine how the Sixers approach Clingan and Robert Williams III inside. The Sixers have leaned on smaller lineups and reserve contributors while Nurse has managed injuries across the roster. Monday could give him more options, even if Embiid cannot play. What Vegas thinks FanDuel Sportsbook listed the Sixers as 3.5-point favorites Monday afternoon. Philadelphia was -152 on the moneyline, Portland was +128 and the over-under was 229.5. The Blazers are 7-4 on the road. The Sixers are 7-2 at Xfinity Mobile Arena. After 17 games within their own conference, the Sixers will finally see what their early success looks like against the other side.

stories.title: Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double
stories.summary: The Sixers improved to 3-0 Saturday night by beating the Bucks at Xfinity Mobile Arena.
stories.detailText: Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers stayed unbeaten Saturday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena, earning a 127-116 win over the Bucks and improving to 3-0 on the season. Joel Embiid had his 10th career regular-season triple-double, tallying 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists. On his 30th birthday, Jaylen Brown posted 27 points and five assists. Tyrese Maxey had 26 points. VJ Edgecombe scored 17 and grabbed 13 boards. The Sixers’ absences on the first night of a back-to-back included LeBron James (low back/sciatica management). Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said pregame that he did not know yet who would be available for his team’s matchup with the Pistons on Sunday. Here are observations on the Sixers’ victory Saturday: Wade debuts, Embiid starts in style Dean Wade made his Sixers debut and started in James’ place. He’d missed the first two games of the regular season with a left ankle sprain. The 3-and-D forward scored the night’s first points by a sinking a corner three-pointer on the opening possession. Embiid also had a sharp start. He moved well, made good decisions and served as the main hub of his team’s offense in the early going. The Sixers’ seven-time All-Star center has often enjoyed facing Myles Turner. He entered the night with an average of 29.4 points in 18 previous games against the Bucks big man. Embiid did a little bit of everything in the first quarter, posting eight points, four assists and four rebounds over nine minutes. After snatching an offensive board, Embiid drained a fadeaway jumper to give the Sixers a 10-1 lead. One of Embiid’s assists was quite stylish. He found Edgecombe open beyond the arc with a behind-the-back bounce pass. Edgecombe knocked down the shot and wound up going 3 for 4 from three-point range in the first quarter. Second-quarter struggles The Sixers added rookie Labaron Philon Jr. to their rotation. Jabari Walker stayed in the mix, though he didn’t enter until the 7:36 mark of the second quarter. Philon played four minutes in his NBA debut and missed his lone shot attempt, a corner three. On defense, Philon allowed a couple of blow-bys off the dribble. He generally looked like he belonged on offense, albeit without any production in his brief run. Maxey banked in a half-court heave at the first-quarter buzzer to put the Sixers up nine points. The Sixers couldn’t carry forward any momentum, however, and began the second quarter poorly. Adem Bona had another rough stint amid a subpar start to the season. After Anfernee Simons missed a transition layup try, Ryan Rollins’ three lifted the Bucks into a 40-37 lead. The dreadful stretch for the Sixers on both sides of the ball called to mind how they’d fallen into a 29-point deficit Thursday night vs. the Cavaliers before clawing out a comeback win. The Sixers mustered just seven points in first six minutes of the second quarter and had many stagnant possessions that concluded with contested jumpers. The team’s transition defense was dismal for much of the second period. Milwaukee had the game’s first 19 fast-break points. Star trio produces The Sixers regained the lead late in the second quarter. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope made two three-balls in the second and nabbed three first-half steals. Embiid assisted a go-ahead, and-one Walker layup. Brown hit a three with 11.8 seconds left in the second quarter. Unsurprisingly, his variety of shotmaking skills were useful without James in the lineup. Even when James or Embiid sit, the Sixers should have a simple advantage in terms of volume of stars over most opponents this year. None of Brown, Embiid or Maxey had the sort of off night that would have improved the Bucks’ odds of a road win. They’d all passed the 20-point mark by the end of the third quarter. Maxey notched another final-possession bucket, this time with a more conventional make. He canned a jumper from the right elbow with 1.7 seconds left in the third to extend the Sixers’ lead to 97-87. The Bucks made a late push in the fourth quarter. Kel’el Ware’s put-back, and-one layup cut the Milwaukee’s deficit to 117-114. The Sixers ultimately handled business. Embiid reached his triple-double by assisting a second-chance Brown jumper and and Caldwell-Pope soon drilled a dagger corner three. Embiid even threw down a last-minute dunk for good measure. For the second consecutive season, the Sixers have a 3-0 start. They got to four wins last year before dropping their first game.

stories.title: Observations after Sixers' 5-game win streak ends with blowout loss to Blazers
stories.summary: The Sixers’ five-game winning streak was snapped by the Trail Blazers.
stories.detailText: Observations after Sixers' 5-game win streak ends with blowout loss to Blazers originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers’ five-game winning streak was snapped Monday night by the Trail Blazers. With a 128-111 defeat at Xfinity Mobile Arena, the Sixers dropped their first game of the year against Western Conference opposition and fell to 14-4. Portland improved to 11-6. LeBron James had a season-high 23 points and six rebounds. Tyrese Maxey scored 22 points and Jaylen Brown added 20. Deni Avdija led the Blazers with 31 points and seven assists. Donovan Clingan posted 15 points and 18 rebounds. The Sixers were missing Joel Embiid (illness). Ja Morant (left hamstring strain) and Shaedon Sharpe (right knee meniscus surgery) were among Portland’s sidelined players. Next on the Sixers’ schedule is a Wednesday night game vs. the Heat. Here are observations on their blowout loss to the Blazers: Walker starts, Brown back in lineup Jabari Walker, listed at 6-foot-7, defied conventional wisdom by winning the opening tip-off against the 7-2 Cllingan. Maxey then canned a three-pointer. Brown scored the Sixers’ next four points with a pair of free throws and a short jumper. VJ Edgecombe’s layup gave the team a 9-2 lead. Brown and Dean Wade both returned Monday after sitting out the last two games with left hamstring injuries. Avdija got hot in the first quarter. He scored 11 quick points, made his first four field goals and helped the Blazers avoid a serious early deficit. The Sixers took a 32-30 edge with 9.3 seconds left in the first when Walker jammed in a put-back dunk. The former Portland second-round draft pick played 17 minutes in his second start of the season and continued to look deserving of a rotation spot. He posted 10 points and five rebounds. Nurse tries different center options Adem Bona was available again following an eight-game absence with a cervical spine sprain. However, Dominick Barlow checked in first to back up Walker. Barlow had an outstanding start to his night. He scored a clever lefty push shot over Clingan and threw down a dunk in the first quarter. Barlow also made a highlight defensive play in his opening stint, defending Avdija in isolation and rejecting his layup attempt. Bona then subbed in for Barlow with 3:23 left in the first quarter. He had a positive first possession, grabbing an offensive rebound and driving in for a dunk. Wade later played at center, too. Barlow logged 16 minutes and had six points. Bona recorded four points and two boards in five minutes. Sixers head coach Nick Nurse ended up using a 10-man rotation and did not play rookie guard Labaron Philon Jr. until fourth-quarter garbage time. Overall, the Sixers’ defense remained considerably worse without Embiid . The team also conceded 15 offensive rebounds, including five to Clingan. “I think your rim protection and ability to do that with some size is always a focal point of being really good defensively,” Nurse said. “And then you’ve got to do it a little bit by committee (with Embiid out). I thought, for the most part, I was looking at possessions where I liked our help into the paint. They were doing a good job of zinging it out. “I didn’t particularly like our (defense) back out. … There were a couple of times they missed those and still got rebounds. We were compacted in the lane with everybody because we didn’t get back out, and then still giving up an offensive rebound as well. That’s just playing through the possession, a little bit of energy, all that kind of stuff. … We just didn’t do enough pieces well.” Downward trend for Sixers’ defense Brown delivered tons of efficient offense for the Sixers in the first half and sure didn’t appear rusty. His layup late in the second quarter tied the game at 58-all. The five-time All-Star scored 19 first-half points on 8-for-10 shooting. Avdija exceeded Brown’s production, hitting heat-check threes, leaners through contact and just about everything he put up regardless of the defender. He tallied 25 points in the first half and shot 9 for 12 from the field. James reached 16 points when he capped a high-scoring half by nailing a corner three. The contest was even at 69 apiece heading into halftime. Monday’s game was James’ first of the season with three or more made three-pointers. The four-time MVP went 4 for 5 beyond the arc. He’d gone 10 for 46 (21.7 percent) over his first 13 games and was due for a good long-range night. James was whistled for his third foul early in the third quarter. Brown picked up his fourth with 10:15 to go in the period, forcing him to sit for an extended stretch. “I wasn’t too happy about it. … I think that affected the game,” Brown said. “It also affected my rhythm a little bit in the second half. I had to sit (almost) the whole third quarter. Coming back from injury, coming back from a hamstring thing, my body didn’t really feel the same after that.” Brown noted postgame that he had “a little bit of soreness and stuff like that.” “I think everything will check out,” he said. “The medical staff is on top of everything. Those hamstrings are tricky, so you want to make sure you play it the right way, be safe. I also don’t want to miss a lot of games, so I might be out there, but I’ve also got to be smart. I think I played it the right way today.” Avdija stopped lighting up the Sixers in the third period, but the team still had another unimpressive defensive quarter. Portland posted 32 points in the third and built its lead to double figures in the opening minute of the fourth. The game devolved into a blowout. An Avdija dunk put the Blazers’ advantage at 22 points with 5:15 on the clock and the Sixers didn’t have a miracle comeback in store. Even with all their wins, there’s no question the Sixers have been trending downward on defense over the past couple of weeks, allowing regular dribble penetration and plenty of comfortable threes. They’ll aim to raise their level on that side of the floor and expect Embiid’s presence to be a major help once he’s back in action. “I think it’s just mindset,” Walker said. “We’re capable when we want to. You need games like this every now and then just to remind you that it’s not as easy as it feels sometimes. It takes effort every game. “I think we can learn a lot from this. It’s just part of the growing pains, but I’m confident we’ll get back to that (early-season) level of defense. We have what it takes.”

Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Rocky Widner/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Having the Spurs well represented at All-Star Weekend the last few years has been a new feeling, and I’m not just talking about the Rising Stars Challenge or the main event. Stephon Castle and Carter Bryant came in as runners up in the Dunk Contest the last two years, marking San Antonio’s first representation there since the 1980’s. Victor Wembanyama also participated in the Skills Challenge in both his rookie and sophomore campaigns (to not-so-great results, as Anthony Edwards’ horsing around cost Team Top Pick the first time, then Wemby and Chris Paul’s attempts to cheese it got them disqualified in the second go-round.) But one event the Spurs have always felt underrepresented at is the Three-Point Contest. Despite being one of the teams that helped to revolutionize the three-pointer and often having some of the top shooters in the league, their history there is limited to Steve Smith (2002), Roger Mason (2009), Matt Bonner (2013) and Marco Belinelli (2014 winner, 2015). And Bonner basically had to plead and even campaign for himself to get in. The Spurs have had many more deserving participants than that, but it’s no lie that the league likes to go for trendier names since these events suffer enough for viewership as it is, and this is an event superstars can participate in without fear of injury or overexertion. Perhaps the most obvious gimmick ever was allowing Damian Lillard to participate last season despite not playing in a single game while recovering from a ruptured Achilles. Was he medically cleared to shoot threes? Of course. Was it a feel-good story? It was, but was it fair to perhaps another deserving participant who played the whole season and otherwise missed out on some bonus money? That is the ultimate question, and I can easily name one such player: Julian Champagnie. Champagnie is the ultimate feel-good story himself. Undrafted out of St. Johns, he signed a two-way contract with the 76ers in 2022, just to be waived for Mac McClung, whom they only wanted to represent them at the Dunk Contest before he was waived himself. Their loss was the Spurs’ gain, and they quickly grabbed him to help with their lack of shooters, and he’s been filling that gap beautifully ever since. Whether starting or coming off the bench, he has always been one of the steadier hands in the NBA. Even though he initially began last season off the bench, he kept finding himself filling in for injured starters before eventually taking over the starting power forward position for good, after Harrison Barnes fell into a slump he couldn’t escape, and it became obvious that having Champangie out there either took defensive pressure off Wemby, or defenders forgot about him and left him wide open. More often than not, he made them pay by hitting 38.1% on over six attempts per game. That shooting carried over into the playoffs, where he hit 39.6% of his threes as a starter for a team that made the finals. This year has been even more of the same in terms of being in and out of the starting lineup, except he’s shooting even better. While it’s still early, he’s currently shooting 41.7% on 7 attempts per game, both career highs. Because the season is still young, that “only” places him at 38th in the league in three-point percentage, but amongplayers who have played in the majority of games and are shooting at least 7 attempts per game, that places him behind only Desmond Bane, Duncan Robinson, Klay Thompson, Steph Curry, Grayson Allen and Jamal Murray. That’s six players, and the contest has eight participants. Odds are as the season progresses, the real shooters of the league will begin to separate themselves, and Champagnie will be one of them. With the Spurs having all the eyes on them now, surely the league will want them well represented at All-Star Weekend. While Wemby is a shoo-in for the All-Star game itself, no one else really is, so maybe putting their best shooter in the Three-Point Contest will be a good start. If Champagnie keeps this up, he’ll be more than deserving, and hopefully it won’t take a Matt Bonner campaign to get it done, but in case it does, we’re starting it right here. Today is November 24, 2026, and with the zero power I have, I am officially nominating Julian Champagnie for the 2027 Three-Point Contest in the Footprint Center in Phoenix, Arizona on Feburary 20. Who’s with me?
