Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Rocky Widner/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The absence of God will bring you comfort, baby. It’s the first thing Jenny Lewis sings on Rilo Kiley’s song of the same name, off 2004’s More Adventurous , and it was stuck in my head all through this sleepy Monday night tilt in Sacramento. The title sounds like a hymn, but the song is more of a wistful little folk tune about love and everything we tell ourselves just to make it to the next day. Lewis, clear and unshowy, sings that opening line like she’s talked herself into it. It’s a soft-spoken battle cry that leaves you torn between rallying behind it and finding a window to look pensively out of. Victor Wembanyama’s brief absence from the lineup shouldn’t inspire this kind of existential wondering though. If ever there were going to be a DNP (Rest) for our Talisman, the first night of a road trip against the worst team in the league has to be at the top of the list. He is not really injured, not in any way that matters. He’s just enjoying a night off from Domantas Sabonis’s elbows rocking into his gut. This wasn’t going to be a hard game. It wasn’t going to be a stressful game. If anything, the absence of Vic did bring comfort, but only in the sense that any outcome could be written off and ignored completely. Without our tallest boy, this game was nothing more than a fixed data point, an entry in that great Excel spreadsheet in the sky, there to remind future generations that on this day in 2026 a basketball game was played. No one can ever say it wasn’t. With stakes like that, you can forgive the mind for going on walkabout, wandering through other rooms of the house to see if anybody is chatting about something, anything even remotely more interesting than whether Zach LaVine can get buckets. The Spurs missed their first four shots, which meant nothing. It sat in my stomach anyway. With a minute and a half left in the first quarter, Malik Monk hit a three and the free throw that came with it, a four-point play that put the Kings up 28-16. A twelve-point deficit. I was checking my phone. Feeding my dogs. A glance back to the screen and there was Fox in a suit. Harper in a suit. Vic in a suit. The Spurs closed the gap to nine on a Kornet free throw as I looked out the window, pensively. In the song, Jenny sings about dressing up your life in different outfits, arrangements, and routines. The absence of God means you can do whatever you want, right? The lack of formal structure or rules provides its own kind of freedom. We can be daytime drunks if we want. We can pretend we’re rich. Maybe it doesn’t fix what’s wrong, but it’s something to do. A Kornet alley-oop off a Castle pass. Then another dunk for Luke, this one off a Gillespie lob. Every Spurs fan I know right now is bracing during the Luke Kornet minutes. Whenever Vic leaves the floor, the team seems to collapse under the weight of the Luke Kornet minutes. Tonight, though, he’s grabbing rebounds. He’s playing perfect defense. He’s hitting outlet passes. He’s beautiful and he’s fun and he’s having his best game of the season. When I look at him I feel nothing but dread. Champagnie just hit his sixth three of the night and the Spurs have the lead back. By the break, they’re up nine. And I say, “There’s trouble when everything is fine” The need to destroy things creeps up on me every time And just as love’s silhouette appears I close my eyes and disappear, tonight The game wove in and out of itself as the second half wore on. The Spurs lead by 12. They lead by 22. They lead by 8. They won by 16. A chart that went up and down. Numbers and data points fixed into place. As they have 15 times this year, the Spurs won and then said their goodbyes. I don’t think I actually enjoyed any of it. I woke up this morning trying to shake off whatever malaise had overcome me during that game. I wanted to write something fun or clever, a quick note on a lark of a game that shouldn’t matter. Nothing rang true. The scoreline was positive, the win was easy, and I felt empty. I think it’s easier to focus on what isn’t there. What isn’t clicking. No one can ever take that away from you, right? The Spurs only seem to beat up on teams who are missing their stars. Without Victor, the team tends to look average at best. They keep blowing leads. The three-guard lineup can’t last forever. Maybe Luka is going to tear us apart. Maybe the Thunder owe us one. Or the Rockets. Or the Wolves. It’s certainly possible that I just don’t want to get my hopes up again. That I’m at war with myself because I feel stupid or embarrassed for getting caught up in the excitement of it all like a child and then having my feelings ripped to shreds because of a basketball game. You know, like a child. The thought of that pain makes the cynical turn so, so easy. It’s right there for you, beckoning you in from the cold of uncertainty to sit down next to it in the relative warmth of despair. They can’t hurt you if you hurt yourself first. Stay two steps ahead of the haters. You think our team sucks? Not as much as I do. Maybe it feels bad to lose, but man, it sure does feel good to be right. There’s dignity in that. Solace, even. The absence of God will bring you comfort, baby. Takeaways Julian Champagnie’s ability to turn into prime Klay Thompson at any given moment is such a perplexing thing for me. On the one hand, oh my god. What found money is this, that a guy we picked up off the scrap heap can become the greatest shooter on the planet one out of every 16 quarters he plays? What a blessing! What manna from heaven! On the other hand, it makes me nervous to get too enamored with it, because he simply can’t do it every night. It’s not his fault! He shouldn’t be doing it at all! But, like, it’s so easy to fall into the trap of thinking the Spurs are unbeatable when Jules shoots like this, because, duh. The question is always going to be where they find points when he doesn’t. I’m probably all set on the Barnes-at-center minutes. We’re good. No, please, I couldn’t possibly have another bite. I’m stuffed. Thank you though. Castle slowly but surely building that three-point percentage back up. We love to see it, but, crucially, nobody talk about it or look directly at it so we don’t scare it away. I SAID DON’T LOOK AT IT! I really do need to pull myself together and stop being so morose all the time. It’s a bad look, especially against a team like Sacramento that might actually be cursed. Look at these guys over at Kang Gang Pod! They’re having so much freakin’ fun, and I’m over here writing essays based on emo lyrics from when I was in high school, smh. Why have we played the Spurs three times? 😭🎶 pic.twitter.com/j3GwaS5CXw — Kang Gang Pod (@KangGangPod) November 24, 2026 WWL Post Game Press Conference I feel like, from a moving-the-needle perspective, there’s no way this one was a crowd pleaser. Yeah, and look, I apologize for that. I’m sure that after a win, everyone wants to come on here and do a bit of celebrating, and I had to drag us down into the muck. Is there a reason you’re not able to just relax and have fun with it right now? I mean, I’m a Virgo, so there’s that. Explains a lot, actually. Mutable earth sign, so it’s in your nature to be practical and grounded. For sure. A witchy lady I work with once told me that, because of my natal placements, I have Pluto in Scorpio and Neptune in Capricorn, which tends to lend itself to a certain generational dread, and I gotta say, that really locked a lot of things in place for me. Oh, well yeah. I mean, there’s nothing you can do about hte natal placements. Believe me, I’ve tried.

stories.title: Longtime Lions owner Martha Firestone Ford dies at age 101
stories.summary: Martha Firestone Ford, who served as the primary owner of the Lions from 2014 to 2020, has died at the age of 101, the team announced Tuesday night.
stories.detailText: Martha Firestone Ford, who served as the primary owner of the Detroit Lions from 2014 to 2020, has died at the age of 101, the team announced Tuesday night. "Over more than six decades with the Detroit Lions, she was a loyal and constant fixture of the franchise, sharing in its history and traditions," the team said in a statement announcing her death. "She remained present with the team even this season, attending games with a devotion that endured throughout her life." No cause of death was given, although the team said she died at home surrounded by her family. Ford and her husband, William Clay Ford Sr., bought the Lions in 1963, and she took over his controlling interest in the team after his death in 2014. Although she seldom spoke to reporters or commented publicly on the direction of the franchise, her influence was felt. She was in charge of the team from 2014 until 2020, when she turned the Lions over to her daughter, Sheila Ford Hamp. Ford had since served as chair emeritus. The Lions made the playoffs in 2014 but lost seven of their first eight games the following season. In November 2015, the team fired its president and general manager in a midseason shake-up. When Ford announced the changes, she told fans the franchise intended to "identify and hire the very best leadership in order to produce a consistently, winning football team." The Lions played better down the stretch that season, and after hiring Bob Quinn as their new general manager, they returned to the playoffs a year later. Although Ford kept a low profile, the shakeup in the middle of the 2015 campaign was a sign that she was more than willing to bring about change in an effort to reverse the team's fortunes. Then-coach Jim Caldwell said she was very much a presence within the organization. "I think visible ownership is great, and Mrs. Ford does it extremely well," Caldwell said in 2015. "She's there before games and she's there after games, and I think guys enjoy that part of it. She comes to practice and things of that nature, so it's been fun." Ford also made an impact in the Detroit community. She was an officer on the board for Detroit Lions Charities and on the board of the Henry Ford Health System. Martha and William Clay Ford were credited with helping establish the Maplegrove Center, a substance abuse treatment facility in West Bloomfield. Born Sept. 16, 1925, in Akron, Ohio, Martha Parke Firestone was a granddaughter of tire magnate Harvey Firestone. She graduated from Vassar College in 1946 and married William Clay Ford Sr., Henry Ford's grandson, the next year. In 2017, Forbes estimated her net worth at more than $1.4 billion. She is survived by her four children, 14 grandchildren and 17 great-grandchildren. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.title: Tommy DeVito embracing latest chance to be NFL starting QB
stories.summary: "Tommy Cutlets" has been in this spot before.
stories.detailText: “Tommy Cutlets” has been in this spot before. Former Giants quarterback Tommy DeVito, who became a household name in New York, is getting another chance to be in the pressure cooker as a starting signal caller . This time his task is to replace the injured Drake Maye, who suffered a fractured right fibula in the Patriots’ blowout loss to the Lions in Germany on Nov. 15. Maye is expected to be out at least six weeks, and though head coach Mike Vrabel hopes Maye can return at some point of the season, it’s no guarantee he will be ready to return for New England in 2026. Tommy DeVito, who is replacing injured starter Drake Maye, is all smiles as he talks to reporters during a news conference before the Patriots’ practice on Nov. 24, 2026, in Foxborough, Mass. AP Either way, the chances of the Patriots (5-5), who are coming off a bye, to make the playoffs will hinge on how well DeVito plays, and that starts Sunday with a road test against the 1-9 Chargers, who suffered a loss to the Jets this past week. “Everybody has embraced me from the first snap and first play I had last week (in the loss to Detroit),” DeVito told reporters, referring to an outing in which he struggled , completing just 12 of 24 for 81 yards with one interception and a fourth-quarter touchdown pass to Lan Larison. “I’ve put my best foot forward in trying to earn their trust.” During the 2023 season with the Giants, DeVito, a northern New Jersey native, showed he can provide a spark when he was forced into the lineup after Daniel Jones and Tyrod Taylor suffered injuries. In that six-game span, “Tommy Cutlets” led Big Blue to three straight victories in which he became the first undrafted free agent rookie since 1970 to have three consecutive games with a passer rating higher than 100. But he couldn’t sustain the strong play and was benched again by Brian Daboll for a once-again healthy Taylor during a loss to the Eagles later in the season. DeVito, who is 3-5 as a starter, started two games for Big Blue in the 2024 season after the Giants benched and waived Jones, but an arm injury and concussion sent him to the sidelines as Drew Lock started the final six games. He became the odd man out after the Giants signed veterans Russell Wilson and Jameis Winston and following the selection of Jaxson Dart in the first round of the 2025 draft. The Giants cut DeVito that summer but hoped to re-sign him to the practice squad after he cleared waivers. Instead, he was claimed by the Patriots. DeVito spent the 2025 season on the practice squad behind Maye and Josh Dobbs but then supplanted Dobbs as Maye’s backup when Dobbs was released. He signed a two-year extension worth up to $7.4 million with $2 million guaranteed. Tommy DeVito throws a pass during the Patriots’ Week 10 loss to the Lions in Germany. Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Vrabel knows the intangible spark DeVito can bring to a team, but says the time he had working with the Patriots’ wide receivers during training camp will benefit him, as well as the starters’ reps he has received this week. “A lot of energy. I think a lot of work in there with those guys,” Vrabel said. “I think he’s taken advantage of his opportunities. I think he’s also improved, just fundamentally. … Those things probably didn’t show up with the exposure from his last game and when he got into it. But I think being able to see some of these things, work on them, focus on them and understand what it is that he can do a little bit better, I think that that’ll obviously help him and in turn, help us.″ DeVito — who said offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels and quarterbacks coach Ashton Grant “want me to be me,” — is pumped up for his latest chance to lead a team as a starter. “You feel more energized for sure. It’s time to go. Injuries are part of the game, unfortunately. For the players that are in that position, that’s how you get opportunities,” DeVito said. — with AP

stories.title: Colts coaches weigh in on Anthony Richardson’s abrupt return to the starting lineup
stories.summary: Colts QB Anthony Richardson will be reinserted into a challenging starting situation, but will get an opportunity to prove himself again—and his complete story in Indianapolis still remains unwritten.
stories.detailText: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 21: Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor #28 celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the third quarter with teammate Anthony Richardson #5 and Head coach Shane Steichen against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium — September 21, 2025 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Dylan Buell/Getty Images) | Getty Images After the surprising release of starting quarterback Daniel Jones, Indianapolis Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr. now receives one last opportunity to prove he’s a viable QB1 for the franchise going forward. As long as he can stay healthy, he projects to start these dismantled 3-8 Colts’ final six games down the stretch of the 2026 campaign. The former 4th overall pick of the 2023 NFL Draft has only started 15 games since being selected by Indianapolis, and his last start for the Colts occurred on December 22, 2024, against the Tennessee Titans. The reason being because of both lengthy injury recovery timelines and a demotion in favor of Jones, until the latter’s surprising recent release. When asked about his rumored “rocky” relationship with Richardson Sr., and his thoughts on Richardson’s long awaited return to the starting lineup, Steichen downplayed any lingering issues and told the local media on Monday ( via The Athletic’s James Boyd ): “I think we’re in a really good place,” Steichen said recently. “I know there is a lot of stuff out there, but me and him, we still talk regularly, and I’m excited for his opportunity. He’s matured over these years. He puts in good work, and now he gets another opportunity, and I’m really looking forward to seeing him go out and compete.” Meanwhile, Colts offensive coordinator Jim Bob Cooter commented on Richardson Sr.’s last four seasons with Indianapolis, noting that being able to reflect and watch from afar could help him take another step forward: #Colts OC Jim Bob Cooter on Anthony Richardson Sr.: "We've obviously had an interesting four years at (QB). But Anthony's got to watch a lot of different guys go through their weekly process … of preparing for an opponent." "It can be nice to have that 10,000 foot view. …" — James Boyd (@RomeovilleKid) November 24, 2026 That being said, Richardson Sr. may have to rely on his still elite athleticism, dual-threat mobility, and improvisation more than ever because he’ll be returning to the first-team offense in less than an ideal situation. He won’t exactly be placed in a position to succeed, as the Colts have been stripped to the studs following early November’s trade deadline. Along the offensive line, the Colts traded All-Pro left guard Quenton Nelson and now have a rookie starting in his place, with both starting left tackles out because of injuries during last Thursday night’s blowout loss in Houston. Meanwhile, this isn’t Hall of Famers Marvin Harrison and Reggie Wayne that he’ll be throwing to, as Indianapolis’ starting receiving corps more closely resembles a patchwork positional group you’d find in preseason. The group has recently struggled to separate, get open, and create any sort of big plays downfield. Perhaps, Richardson with his ability to run, create plays outside the pocket, and willingness to throw downfield can provide a spark for this stagnant Colts offense, which mustered just 3 points last Thursday night. If nothing else, he should be more exciting on offense, as the prior disastrous Daniel Jones led offense in 2026 had clearly run its course this season, and a change at the position was long overdue.

(Photo by Steven King/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Detroit Lions announced on Tuesday night that former team owner Martha Firestone Ford has passed away at age 101. According to the team, she passed away at her home surrounded by family. Ford took over as principal owner of the franchise in 2014, following the death of her husband, William Clay Ford. She held onto the role until 2020, when she bequeathed primary ownership to her daughter and current Lions owner Sheila Hamp. Since then, Ford has been serving as Owner/Chair Emeritus of the team. Here’s how the team described her role over the past six years. In her most recent role as Owner/Chair Emeritus, Mrs. Ford supported her four children – Principal Owner/Chair Sheila Ford Hamp, Owner/Vice Chair Martha Ford Morse, Owner/Vice Chair William Clay Ford Jr., and Owner/Vice Chair Elizabeth Ford Kontulis – as they assumed leadership responsibilities within the family franchise. Today the Ford family proudly carries forward the legacy established by Mr. and Mrs. Ford, preserving the values, love, and passion that have shaped a family tradition spanning multiple generations. During Mrs. Ford’s brief stint as primary owner, the Lions made the playoffs twice (2014, 2016) and produced three winning seasons. The team offered this official statement on Ford’s passing: “It is with heavy hearts that we acknowledge the passing of Martha Firestone Ford. Mrs. Ford inspired us all as a pillar of the Detroit community and the passionate matriarch of the Detroit Lions football team. “She will always be remembered for her fierce loyalty to her family, her community, and the city of Detroit. “Her presence on our sideline, in our building, and in our community will be greatly missed. stories.title: Broncos' Sean Payton: J.K. Dobbins suspended one game for detrimental conduct
stories.summary: The Broncos suspended running back J.K. Dobbins for one game for conduct detrimental to the team.
stories.detailText: ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- Denver Broncos coach Sean Payton said Tuesday that he has suspended running back J.K. Dobbins for Friday's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers due to "conduct detrimental.'' Dobbins will not practice or take part in any team activities this week. The Broncos (8-2) face the Steelers on Friday at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh. "There is one team announcement, I'm not going to comment afterwards: I'm suspending J.K. Dobbins for this weekend's game, conduct detrimental, that's all I'm going to say about it,'' Payton said after Tuesday's practice. "Head coach's decision.'' Asked if he wanted to elaborate on any of the circumstances that surrounded the decision, Payton said no and added "think it's better that way.'' Dobbins was in the Broncos' facility earlier Tuesday and then left, multiple team sources said. Payton then told players of the suspension in the team's normally scheduled group meeting. Dobbins, in his second season with the team and a player Payton had called one of the "top priorities'' to re-sign this past offseason, had one carry, for no gain, in the Broncos' 38-24 victory Sunday over the Las Vegas Raiders . It marked the first time since the 2020 season Dobbins had a single carry in a game he was in uniform to play -- he had two one-carry games for the Baltimore Ravens that year. Dobbins was visibly frustrated at times on the sideline during Sunday's game and high-fiving teammates at other times. When asked about the running back rotation Monday, Payton had offered that Dobbins "is healthy'' and that "J.K. is going to be super important for what we're doing in this stretch.'' Jonah Coleman , who sat out four games earlier this season because of an ankle injury, has steadily received more work since his Week 7 return to the lineup. Coleman got 24 of the team's 27 carries by running backs Sunday. Coleman's 111 yards rushing were also the team's first 100-yard rushing game since Dobbins' 111 in a Week 8 win last season over the Dallas Cowboys . The Broncos also designated running back Tyler Badie for return from injured reserve Tuesday, and he practiced with the team and was listed as a full participant. Asked if Badie would play Friday or how the rotation might look against the Steelers, Payton said, "I'm not going to get into who's playing.'' Running back RJ Harvey (knee) is eligible to return from injured reserve next week. Quarterback Bo Nix , when asked about the suspension, said: "Well, obviously I have nothing to do with it,'' Nix said. "Just keep finding our way to figure out how to win games, fortunately it has nothing to do with me.'' Cornerback Pat Surtain II , also a team captain like Nix, offered a similar answer with, "I ain't got nothing much to say, it's coach's decision at the end of the day.'' It's all a long way from Dobbins' promise -- he termed it a "pinkie swear'' -- both during the team's minicamp in June as well as training camp, that he would play in every game this season and lead the league in rushing. "This year, forget a top-three, I keep saying it, people think I'm crazy but I'm going to be No. 1, and I'm going to keep it there for the whole year,'' Dobbins said in August. "You know, 17 games. A lot of people get mad when I say the injuries are over, cause I said it last year, but that one was pretty fluky, right? This year there won't be any.'' Dobbins has dealt with several injuries in his career, including a career-threatening knee injury, and he sat out the final seven regular-season games because of a foot injury as well as both of the Broncos' playoff games last season. His 15 games played in 2020, as a rookie for the Baltimore Ravens, is still the most games he has played in a season. It is believed Dobbins, who signed a two-year, $16 million deal with the team this past offseason, is the first player suspended by the Broncos during a season for conduct detrimental to the team since wide receiver Brandon Marshall in 2009.

stories.title: No, the Chicago Bears are Not in Salary Cap Hell
stories.summary: Don’t be a dope by listening to people who don’t understand the NFL salary cap. The Bears’ situation is fine.
stories.detailText: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: General manager Ryan Poles of the Chicago Bears walks the field prior to the game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images Yesterday, someone shared on social media (no, I won’t elevate their account here) that the Chicago Bears had a dire salary cap situation looming in 2027. It’s not the biggest account, and it’s not even a sports-related account, but it picked up a bunch of traction as others shared it. Some believed the erroneous content and complained the Bears were screwed or wanted to lol at the stupid Bears, while others wanted to dunk on how wrong the take was. A prominent gambling account (I won’t elevate this account either) picked up on the narrative and, to gain clicks and engagement, shared their own version of the “oh no, the Bears are in cap Hell in 2027!” tweet to all their followers too. For those not on social media, Bears fans are an easy mark. And that’s not meant negatively; our fanbase is very, very active and passionate, and if you want to bait us or troll us, you’re going to get a reaction. ESPN’s Field Yates, who knows a thing or two about the NFL and the salary cap, came across that above-referenced tweet and shared , “I don’t know why this notion that the Bears are facing salary cap straits in 2027 has generated traction recently, but it’s… not true. There are so many pathways for this team to easily clear cap room next year. And extend Caleb Williams.” Nick Korte, who is a contributor at Over the Cap and one of the best follows for salary cap and comp pick info, responded to Yates with this . Simple restructures of the 5 players who the Bears have already devoted guaranteed salaries to in 2027 gets them in salary cap compliance without doing anything else. stories.title: Paulson Adebo gets shot at Giants redemption after up-and-down season
stories.summary: With Greg Newsome II out 4 to 6 weeks, Giants CB Paulson Adebo reclaims a starting job after an up-and-down season.
stories.detailText: Paulson Adebo looked out of place at practice last week as the NFL’s highest-paid “don’t-forget-about-me” trying to find his place on the punt team. Access the Giants like never before Get texts from Paul Schwartz with all the latest Giants news and insights, exclusive to Sports+ subscribers. tRY IT NOW Two days later, Adebo improbably looked totally at home as a shutdown cornerback whose wild ride this season is about to accelerate further because he has risen from purgatory to again be considered one of the Giants’ most important players. “Obviously, it’s not where I wanted to be going into the season,” Adebo said after Tuesday’s meetings. “You prepare every week like you’re going to play. If you’re the third [cornerback], you’re one play away from going in every game, so you owe it to yourself and you owe it to your teammates to be prepared.” Adebo, whose $24.1 million salary cap charge is the highest on the Giants, lost his starting job to Deonte Banks and Greg Newsome II in training camp. He was picked on off the bench in Week 1, missed the next five games due to injury, returned to play well against the Texans as Banks’ fill-in, was a healthy scratch against the Commanders and then saved the day with four passes defended and an interception after Newsome was injured against the Jaguars. With Newsome now expected to miss four to six weeks due to ankle surgery , Adebo will start opposite Banks on Sunday against the Colts. The Giants will face three of the NFL’s top six passing attacks in that six-game window. New York Giants cornerback Paulson Adebo (21) runs off the field after an interception against the Jacksonville Jaguars in East Rutherford, N.J., Nov. 22, 2026. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect “I know what type of player I am,” Adebo said. “I know what I can do on the field. I know what type of person I am, so I don’t think it’s anything new necessarily that I’ve learned about myself, but certainly just staying prepared and ready to go when you’re called upon.” Only 20 months after signing a three-year, $54 million contract as the prize of the Giants’ 2025 free agent class, Adebo was inactive against the Commanders because backup cornerbacks Colton Hood and Nic Jones offered more special teams value. Adebo played 13 total special teams snaps from 2022-25 as he developed into a starting corner for the Saints and then the Giants’ No. 1 option against elite receivers. Head coach John Harbaugh pulled aside Adebo last week to keep him engaged with a message that turned out to be prescient. New York Giants’ Greg Newsome II (20) runs during training camp at the Greenbrier in White Sulphur Springs, W.Va., Saturday, Aug. 1, 2026. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST “I said, ‘In my mind, you’re a starter in this league. And when you started here, you’ve done really well. And you’re going to have to start again,’ ” Harbaugh said Nov. 18. “So when that time comes, he’s in a good place.” The time came Sunday when Adebo allowed two catches on eight targets. His fourth-quarter interception at the 28-yard line secured three points (to extend to a 14-point lead) at a time when the offense couldn’t move the ball. “I mean, I’m glad that [Harbaugh] thinks that,” Adebo said. “I certainly think highly of myself. So, kind of been thinking that way the whole season. So, it wasn’t anything new per se.” The stretch run of the season suddenly becomes a proving ground for Adebo, who recently looked like a lock to be a salary cap casualty ($14 million saved against $6.3 million dead money) in 2027. Could the Giants feel comfortable with Adebo and Newsome as starters next year if Banks leaves in free agency? “He’s a baller,” safety Jevón Holland said. “He hasn’t been playing that much this year, but it’s just how the game goes. When they called his name, he went out and balled. I’m excited for him.” People snickered when Newsome prematurely declared the Giants cornerback room the best in the NFL during the preseason. It’s become harder to argue with his assessment as time has passed. The performance against Trevor Lawrence was a definitive argument because Banks added an interception and Dru Phillips made three of the most important plays (all breakups) of the game. “I think I said it in training camp about how we have three, four guys that are really starters in this league,” Adebo said. “So, there really is that mindset that we all know we can compete. So, just keep on executing, keep on doing what we’ve been doing.”

Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba running with the ball during an NFL game. stories.title: Bears' Johnson has no plan to stop using Swift in run game despite costly fumbles
stories.summary: Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift won't have an extended stay in Ben Johnson's doghouse after fumbling in the fourth quarter against the Saints.
stories.detailText: LAKE FOREST, Ill. -- Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift won't have an extended stay in Ben Johnson's doghouse after fumbling in the fourth quarter against the Saints. Swift has lost three fumbles through 10 games, which are his most since the 2023 season. The 27-year-old back was pulled from the lineup after New Orleans recovered his fumble at its own 46-yard line and did not return to the game. That's the second time this season Swift has been benched in game after fumbling. Swift's fumbles have gone from an aberration to an issue that has become more frequent than at any other point of his Bears tenure. But when asked Tuesday whether Swift needs to regain the trust of his head coach, Johnson rebuffed the idea. "No, he just needs to hold on to the ball and we'll be fine," Johnson said. The Bears rushed for 146 yards against the Saints, their third-highest output of the season. Still, Johnson was displeased with the run game's efficiency, spotlighted by Swift's 13 carries for 51 yards (3.9 yards per carry). The veteran back also recorded his first touchdown reception of the season. "We weren't as consistent running the ball as we had wanted to be coming off the bye, that was a point of emphasis for us," Johnson said postgame. "When I looked at our runners, they were under four yards a carry. That efficiency stat that we talked about, we weren't hitting that." The Bears' offense centers on a rushing attack that ranks third leaguewide at 142.4 yards per game. That figure would not be possible without Swift, who has played in all 10 games and shouldered a heavier load while running back Kyle Monangai missed five straight weeks with turf toe and a thumb injury. Monangai returned in Week 11 but was limited to eight carries for 18 yards. With a quick turnaround before facing the Lions on Thanksgiving and seeking their first NFC North win, the Bears are quickly searching for a way to get their run game on track. From Johnson's perspective, the solution is right in front of them. "We're going to continue to stress that running game," Johnson said Tuesday. "We got too many good players for it to be lacking behind like it is right now. So, we got to continue to sink into that. It's a big part of what we do and who we are. Whether that's Swift, whether that's Monangai, Salvon [Ahmed] came on and played some big snaps for us. We're going to do that, and we're going to continue to possess the ball and those types of things so that opens up our passing game eventually." Swift ranks 14th in rushing yards (627), and his 10 rushing TDs are tied for the third in the league. He signed a three-year, $33.75 million contract extension with Chicago before Week 1.

stories.title: Report: NFL, YouTube are negotiating a three-game package for 2027

stories.detailText: YouTube's on-again, off-again arrangements to stream select NFL games may be on again. John Ourand of Puck reports in his Varsity newsletter that the NFL and YouTube have been negotiating a three-game package for the 2027 season. The arrangement would include a Christmas Eve game, the Week 17 Saturday game to be televised by NBC, and the Week 10 European game that was televised by Fox. This year, Christmas Eve lands on a Thursday; Prime Video will televise the Texans-Eagles game that night (barring a flex). Next year, Christmas Eve lands on a Friday. YouTube was at one point negotiating the five-game package for 2026 that landed with Netflix. It includes Wednesday night's first-of-its-kind Thanksgiving Eve game between the Packers and Rams. YouTube walked, as Ourand reported at the time, when the league tried to split the five-game package between multiple partners. The arrangement between the NFL and YouTube currently includes Sunday Ticket. That package could be disappearing in the next round of broadcast deals. The inevitable expansion of the regular season to 18 games per team will create another 16 games that can be sliced and diced into special packages.

They’ve already beaten them once the season, and this time around they are the ones with the home-field advantage. To secure the victory this week the Cowboys are going to need some impact plays on both sides of the ball. Today, we identified one offensive and defensive player we believe will make such an impact, helping to sway the game in Dallas’ favor. Offense – WR George Pickens The Cowboys aerial attack has been lethal the past two games and a lot of that probably has to do with George Pickens’ uptick in production. He’s coming off back-to-back 100+ receiving yard games and has been much more involved in Dallas’ passing game during that time. In the last two weeks alone he’s caught 18 passes for 247 yards and four touchdowns. We believe we will see more of the same in the Thanksgiving Day matchup with the Eagles. The Eagles are currently ranked 17 th in the league allowing 222.8 receiving yards per game. They held George Pickens to just four catches for 57 yards in Week 7, but did allow him to score a touchdown in that matchup. That was then and this is now. No. 3 is playing his best football right now and QB Dak Prescott is looking his way more often because of it. Another 100-yard receiving game isn’t out of the question. Defense – LB Justin Barron Dee Winters exited the game early with a knee injury last week against the Titans and didn’t return. The Cowboys surprisingly chose to replace him in the starting lineup with LB Justin Barron, who they signed as an undrafted free agent out of Syracuse last year. He’s predominantly been a special teams player thus far in his young career with the Cowboys, but ended up leading the team in tackles last week with nine as an injury fill-in. With it being a short week, No. 45 has a good chance to get his first NFL career start on Thanksgiving against the Eagles. He was impressive last week while filling in for Dee Winters and could get rewarded because of it. He seems to have the coaching staffs trust and has been productive when given the opportunity. (Photo by Michael Allio/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It’s a glorious week. The Chicago Bears won, albeit ugly, raising their record to 8-2, and they may have the biggest Bears-Lions game coming up on Thanksgiving in the Super Bowl era. The winner of the game will have sole possession of first place and put themselves in prime position to earn the number 2 (possibly, but doubtful, the number 1) seed entering the NFL playoffs. The Bears are a road favorite on Thursday afternoon, but if they are going to win this game, the offense is going to have to play better than it has in the last two games. Yes, the defense should be able to keep the Lions’ explosive attack mostly at bay, but the Lions are still going to almost certainly crack 20 points, so the Bears offense will have to do some scoring of their own. The offense has looked out of sorts, and that’s largely due to the running game not firing the way it should. I firmly believe that if the running game gets going, the passing game will click right along with it, and this offense will start humming like we all know it can. But why is the running game having issues? Many of us (Tom Brady included) thought that the running game was just missing Kyle Monangai, and when he returned, so would the rushing attack. But it didn’t happen. And it didn’t happen against a poor run defense. Yes, Monangai was ineffective, and if he had more success, things could have been better, but why didn’t he have success? Why is D’Andre Swift well below his yards per carry that he averaged last year? I’m not going to pretend I’m Brian Baldinger breaking down the tape, but when I watch the OL play, I watch a combo of Darnell Wright and Jonah Jackson that looks just as effective as it did in 2025. I see Theo Benedet possibly playing the best LT that anyone has played over the last one and a half seasons. Joe Thuney is still a good player, but he definitely isn’t playing as well as he did last season, and that brings us to center. Garrett Bradbury is not playing well; he has not been playing well, and him next to Thuney is definitely the spot in the line that you can circle as the weakness in the running game. You can’t run behind Wright and Jackson every single time; it simply won’t work. Last year with Drew Dalman, the center and guards were doubling, scraping, and getting to the second level at an absolutely fantastic level. The second-level blocks just aren’t there as consistently as they were last year, and I think that’s creating an issue for the rushing attack to be cohesive. The blocking is not awful. If this was the blocking we were getting three or four years ago, we’d all be over the moon, but times have changed, the Bears are trying to win a Super Bowl, and there needs to be an improvement. Don’t get me wrong, there have been other things that have prevented the Bears from running the ball as well; Cole Kmet has been a significant loss. Sam Roush continues to improve, and hopefully in a few more weeks he will be closer to what Kmet was, but he isn’t there yet. So while Bradbury isn’t the only problem, he is one of the problems, and he’s one of the problems that can be fixed. Is it time to try Logan Jones? Transitioning to a different center is a tricky thing to do midseason. You want consistency at the position. A short week is not the right time to switch to a rookie; the bye week would have made sense, but it also could be done with extended time between the Thanksgiving game and the following week. I think the Bears should give Bradbury this game, and if it’s still not working, I think they need to make a change at center. Is Logan Jones ready? He certainly was an experienced college player, so one would hope so. I know Ben Johnson puts a lot on a center’s shoulders, but while Bradbury might be handling the between-the-ears, he certainly isn’t handling the physical. If Jones isn’t ready, is it too crazy to call Drew Dalman and see if he’s still in playing shape and if he’s changed his mind? Those really are the only two options, but here’s what I know: if the run game operates like this as the temperatures get cold and the competition heats up, the Bears aren’t going to win the Super Bowl. Perhaps there’s a way to make this run game work with Bradbury. Ben Johnson is a lot smarter than me, so if there’s anyone who can find a way, it’s Ben. I know he knows the run game is currently unacceptable. But when Ben Johnson says it’s going to be a focal point of the bye week, Kyle Monangai returns, the Bears are playing a poor run defense, and this was the result? It’s time to be a little worried. We are far from panicking; there’s absolutely no reason to do that at this point, but it’s time to start trying a few different things to see if they can make this thing go, and the center position needs to be at or near the top of the list. There’s a lot on the line on Thanksgiving; if the Bears are going to have another statement win on national television, it needs to start with running the football. It’s time for Ben Johnson to separate the men from the boys and make this thing go. Thursday would be the perfect day to start.

stories.summary: Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is scheduled to visit Wednesday with the Commanders, agent Drew Rosenhaus told ESPN's Adam Schefter.
stories.detailText: Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is scheduled to visit Wednesday with the Washington Commanders , agent Drew Rosenhaus told ESPN's Adam Schefter. The San Francisco 49ers released Aiyuk on Tuesday, two weeks after the NFL reinstated him. He cleared waivers, making him an unrestricted free agent. Aiyuk has not played since tearing the ACL, MCL and meniscus in his right knee on Oct. 20, 2024, and was placed on the 49ers' reserve/left squad list last December. He could not be removed from that list until he reported and passed a physical, which he did Nov. 9. "I'm feeling great, feeling healthy," Aiyuk told 49ers reporters earlier this month. "It was a long recovery process, a long rehab process, but I'm back to 100%." Aiyuk is expected to work out for the Commanders during Wednesday's visit. In 2023, his last full season before his injury, Aiyuk was named second-team All-Pro after catching 75 passes for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns. Aiyuk and Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels played together at Arizona State during the 2019 season. However, a rift in their relationship appeared to have developed following a series of social media posts by the receiver. Aiyuk targeted Daniels in several posts and in one referenced Daniels' mother. Daniels and Aiyuk spoke more than a month ago to clear the air, according to multiple sources. Daniels befriended Aiyuk early in their time together at ASU -- before Daniels had won the starting quarterback job. During workouts, Daniels would throw with Aiyuk, who was going into his senior season and coming off a 33-catch, 474-yard season. They quickly developed a rapport as Aiyuk ended the season with Associated Press All-America honors after catching 65 passes for 1,192 yards and eight touchdowns. ESPN's John Keim contributed to this report.

stories.detailText: The Commanders will meet with receiver Brandon Aiyuk on Wednesday, according to a report from ESPN’s Adam Schefter. Citing the information frim agent Drew Rosenhaus, Schefter says Aiyuk will meet with Washington brass on Wednesday. Free-agent WR Brandon Aiyuk is scheduled to visit Wednesday with the Washington Commanders, per his agent Drew Rosenhaus. Aiyuk and Commanders QB Jayden Daniels played together at Arizona State during the 2019 season. https://t.co/5GZRgm9P1D — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 24, 2026 This meeting comes after the 49ers released him on Monday, and Aiyuk then cleared waivers on Tuesday. A long dispute with the 49ers had previously been resolved when he reported to the team after months on the team’s exempt-did not report list . At that time, the NFL gave San Francisco a two-week roster exemption, which expired this week, and which they rook advantage of before finally parting ways. Explaining everything that went wrong between Aiyuk and the 49ers would involve thousands of words, but we can sum it up by saying there was a disagreement about his rehab plans that devolved into a messy situation that left the player and team at odds. Then there was a rash of social media post by Aiyuk slamming 49ers brass, including general manager John Lynch and head coach Kyle Shanahan. Aiyuk also took shots at good friend, former Arizona State teammate and current Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels, but Aiyuk reached out to Daniels and they reportedly squashed their friction . The fact he was even given a meeting with the Commanders supports that claim. Aiyuk has made it clear for months that he wants to sign with Washington — he regularly wears Commanders gear in social media posts — who could use some receiver help with Terry McLaurin done for the year with a torn patellar tendon. Aiyuk is expected to draw interest from a few teams, with a practice squad signing as his likeliest path back to NFL action. stories.title: Week 12 Chicago Bears power rankings roundup
stories.summary: Power rankings are out and @SamHouseholder rounds ‘em up.
stories.detailText: CHICAGO, IL - NOVEMBER 22: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams (18) points during the NFL game between the New Orleans Saints and the Chicago Bears on November 22, 2026, at Soldier Field in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Allio/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Chicago Bears moved to 8-2 with a pretty forgettable win over the New Orleans Saints. But it is quickly on to bigger and better things. The team turns around to face the Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving Day. This week is super compressed and not just the players, but also your bloggers. And this year is even worse because there is a game tomorrow already. Heading into this crucial stretch as the season really starts boiling down to talks of division crowns and playoff seeding, let’s see how the analysts rank the Bears. And with the holiday looming, there is naturally a mostly thankful theme to this week’s rankings by many outlets. WCG – Aaron Leming 5. Chicago Bears (8-2) Reason(s) To Be Thankful: Despite some skepticism, the marriage of Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams has been as advertised (or hoped). Three years ago, when the Bears drafted Williams, it felt like all of their quarterback troubles were going to wash away eventually. Year 1 under former head coach Matt Eberflus went about as expected, but landing the big fish in Johnson the following offseason was a franchise changer. Things didn’t always look pretty last season, but both have worked to establish a winning culture. With Williams taking the next step in Year 3, it feels like the sky is the limit for this team if their defense keeps improving. The Athletic – Chad Graff and Josh Kendall 5. Chicago Bears (8-2) Last week: 6 Sunday: Beat Saints 21-13 Something to be thankful for: The Jeffery Simmons trade Since being traded ahead of Week 8, Simmons has five sacks, which is second in the league in that span. He had three Sunday against the Saints, and it’s not the only way he is contributing. He is making 1.7 splash plays per game since joining the Bears (which also ranks second in the league) thanks to 10 quarterback pressures and a run stuff. “My man crush continues,” Mike Tomlin said on “Sunday Night Football.” “This guy is an apex predator.” Up next: at Lions, Thursday, 1 p.m. ET Yahoo Sports – Frank Schwab 3. Chicago Bears (8-2, LW: 5) The Bears haven’t trailed in five straight games, and that streak brings back memories of the greatest team in franchise history. The last time the Bears went five games without trailing was 1985, when they went the final three games of the regular season and the first two playoff games without trailing, according to Larry Mayer of ChicagoBears.com. The Bears briefly trailed the Patriots 3-0 in Super Bowl XX before winning 46-10. While this version of the Bears is much different than the famous 1985 team, their pass rush is starting to emerge since Jeffery Simmons came aboard in a trade. On Sunday, they sacked the Saints’ Tyler Shough six times (three times by Simmons) and had 24 pressures, which is the most for the team since 2018, according to Next Gen Stats. The defensive improvement will be tested on Thanksgiving in a massive NFC North game against the Lions. USAToday – Nate Davis 2. Chicago Bears (3): They haven’t trailed since QB Caleb Williams’ Week 6 return from a hamstring injury. Could be a tough streak to maintain on Turkey Day in Motown, though. FOX Sports – Ralph Vacchiano 5. Chicago Bears (5) Super Bowl odds: +850 (third) The Bears should have played a lot better than they did in their 21-13 home win over the Saints, especially since New Orleans turned the ball over twice and had a nightmare performance on special teams. But Chicago’s vaunted offense could never really get going, outside of two second-quarter touchdown drives. QB Caleb Williams was just OK. The running game was productive, though top back D’Andre Swift had only 51 yards. This marked the Bears’ fifth straight win, but it honestly looked like they were enjoying the calm before the storm of their Thanksgiving showdown with the Lions in Detroit. They’ll need a much better showing from their offense to have a chance then. This will be the game when we find out if the Bears are who we thought they were all along. CBS Sports – Pete Prisco 3. Chicago Bears (4) The offense hasn’t been humming lately, but the defense has really taken a step forward. The Lions game will be a real test on Thanksgiving. Profootballtalk – Mike Florio 4. Bears (No. 5; 8-2): We’ll learn a lot about this team in Detroit on Thursday. ESPN – NFL Nation – Courtney Cronin 4. Chicago Bears Week 11 result: Beat the Saints 21-13 Week 11 ranking: 4 Extension candidate: QB Caleb Williams Williams becomes eligible for his first extension after this season. He’s the franchise quarterback the Bears searched decades to find, and pairing him with coach Ben Johnson for the foreseeable future is the priority. Chicago’s front office has an incentive to get ahead of a rapidly inflating QB market, which will see the likes of C.J. Stroud and Lamar Jackson come to the table, along with others in Williams’ draft class. Though Williams said in September that “money’s not a motivating factor for me,” his top-10 play on a contending team could lead to him earning around $70 million per year. Signing Williams early would allow the Bears to keep his 2027 cap hit low while prorating a massive signing bonus into future years. — Courtney Cronin NFL.com – Nick Shook 7. Chicago Bears (6) The last few weeks haven’t been the Sunday cruise that the Bears produced earlier this season, but we’ve certainly come to understand just how valuable Jeffery Simmons is to their Super Bowl chase. The recently acquired defensive tackle terrorized the Saints in Sunday’s win, recording three sacks and once again elevating the entire unit. There are still kinks to work out for the Bears — including attempting to locate their rushing attack — but they maintained pace in the NFC North race for another week. What do you think of this week’s rankings? Who is too high and who is too low?

stories.title: JK Dobbins suspended for ‘conduct detrimental’ in mysterious Broncos decision
stories.summary: Broncos coach Sean Payton suspended running back JK Dobbins for Friday's game against the Steelers due to conduct detrimental to the team.
stories.detailText: J.K. Dobbins won’t be suiting up against the Steelers on Friday. Broncos coach Sean Payton was scant with details surrounding the team-imposed one-game ban for his veteran running back. “I’m suspending J.K. Dobbins for this weekend’s game,” he told reporters Tuesday . “Conduct detrimental. That’s all I’m going to say about it. Coach’s decision.” Broncos running back J.K. Dobbins (27) makes a catch against the Carolina Panthers. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The 27-year-old rusher started the season as the Broncos’ No. 1 running back, but has steadily lost time to rookie Jonah Coleman, culminating in Denver’s 38-24 win over the Raiders on Sunday in which Dobbins had one rushing attempt for zero yards to Coleman’s 111 yards and three touchdowns on 24 runs. It marked a career-low in attempts for the eighth-year pro. “We certainly didn’t go in with the idea it was just going to be maybe that one dimensional, but that was the way that game unfolded,” Payton said Monday, adding that Dobbins is healthy and he’s “going to be super important for what we’re doing in this stretch.” What happened in the hours between is a mystery, with Dobbins not taking the field for practice on Tuesday. Earlier in the season, as he ceded touches to Coleman, the Ohio State product became testy with reporters looking for insight . Broncos running back J.K. Dobbins (27) celebrates a touchdown against the Arizona Cardinals. AP Photo/Rick Scuteri “You keep calling me a vet. I’m not old. I’m 27 years old. Not old. I’m not 30. I’m not even close to 30,” Dobbins said as he fielded questions after a 30-16 win over the Cardinals in Week 7. “So, let’s be smart about it. And that’s what it was, I believe. I’m not sure; you guys might make something bigger than what it is, but I’m just here to support my teammates and I love my teammates, and I think they love me too. So, there’s your answer to that.” On the season, Dobbins leads the Broncos with 324 rushing yards and 99 attempts, adding three scores on the ground with nine catches and 34 yards through the air.

He may not be one for long. The former 49ers receiver cleared waivers on Tuesday. Agent Drew Rosenhaus told ESPN that Aiyuk is scheduled to visit the Commanders on Wednesday. Aiyuk has been linked to the Commanders for months. He played college football at Arizona State with quarterback Jayden Daniels. Commanders G.M. teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Kirby Lee/NFLPhotoLibrary) | Getty Images I got the opportunity to sit down and interview actor Simms May, who portrays Michael Madden in the Amazon Prime Video “Madden” movie. You can check out the full interview, From the Set to the Silver and Black: Simms May on “Madden.” Here’s the link. It was a great opportunity to see what happens behind the scenes of movies and talk about the biggest project of a young career. May nailed his role as a young knucklehead with one of the most recognizable dads in America. The most incredible part about his role was that he was unable to meet with any of the Madden family until the night of the premiere. He ultimately achieved the nod of approval and praise from Mr. Michael Madden himself, which is a big deal for an actor making only his fourth appearance on the big screen. When auditioning for the part, Simms didn’t know what the movie was about. In fact, they used the code name Santa Maria’s BBQ. An interesting caveat for any aspiring actors: you won’t know what you are actually auditioning for until you land the role. Locking in and securing the role became the mission for May and he was extremely excited to know what he was participating in when he landed it. Through some of his research and after the creation of the movie, May showed excellent life-decision-making skills in turning towards the dark side and becoming a part of Raider Nation. Making his hometown team, the Atlanta Falcons, rise up and kick rocks. Why? Because he learned about the previously winningest team in NFL history, the greatest organization, with the greatest coaches and “just win, baby.” Famous co-stars On the set, May worked alongside high-level method actors Nicholas Cage (John Madden) and Christian Bale (Al Davis). Detailing throughout the entire shoot, only three times did he come into contact with Nicholas Cage and not Madden, his movie dad. His favorite co-star was none other than Shane Gillis, their movie neighbor and resident funny man. Gillis was the same guy off-set that he was on it, absolutely hilarious. Regrettably, May had concluded the filming of his role prior to Marshawn BeastMode Lynch arriving on set to film his. However, he did get to see current Raiders superstar Maxx Crosby come in, film his role and got to hang out on set. Joy in exploits May is jubilant about being in the Madden movie, indoctrinating himself into such an outstanding fanbase and being able to further his own career all at once. Getting to work with brilliant actors and being on set with a comedian was like unlocking stairs to the next level of personal greatness. Much like the 2026 Raiders, he started at the bottom, but now he’s here.

headlines.title: Kevin Porter Jr. In Talks With Nuggets, Magic
headlines.summary: Free agent guard Kevin Porter Jr. is in talks with the Denver Nuggets and Orlando Magic, sources told Jake Fischer of The Stein Line. Porter has met with both teams, including a visit with the Magic on Monday. Porter, 26, continues to lean toward staying in the NBA, even if it means accepting a minimum-salary contract. Porter could earn more by returning to Europe. The Milwaukee Bucks waived Porter on Oct. 19, the day before the regular season began. Porter appeared in 38 games last season with the Bucks, averaging 17.4 points, 5.2 rebounds and 7.4 assists in 33.2 minutes. Denver has long been interested in Porter. Before his release, the Nuggets tried to trade for him with an offer built around three second-round picks and Zeke Nnaji's contract. Porter played briefly for PAOK Thessaloniki in Greece during the 2023-24 season. Porter is the last of the top free agent guards still available after Gabe Vincent signed a one-year, non-guaranteed deal with the Sacramento Kings on Monday.

headlines.title: Murray and Jokic power Nuggets past Bulls in overtime
headlines.summary: Denver beat Chicago 151–145 in overtime. Murray scored 45 points with six threes, and Jokic had 37 points, 18 rebounds and 11 assists. Josh Giddey gave the Bulls 23 points, 14 rebounds and 22 assists, and Buddy Hield scored 33 with seven threes in the loss. The game was a clear example of two high-scoring teams going to overtime.

headlines.title: Bucks end a 13-game losing streak
headlines.summary: Milwaukee beat Toronto 116–111 to snap a 13-game losing streak. Tyler Herro had 32 points, eight assists and six rebounds, and Myles Turner fouled out with a season-high 27 points and 11 rebounds. Scottie Barnes scored 31 points with four blocks in the loss for Toronto.

headlines.title: Pacers snap four-game skid against Thunder
headlines.summary: Indiana beat Oklahoma City 125–120 behind Pascal Siakam, who had 20 points and a late three-pointer with 44.4 seconds to go. Kelly Oubre Jr. added a season-high 20 points. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 38 for the Thunder, but the loss ended their run of strong form. The Pacers had lost four straight.

headlines.title: Blazers beat the 76ers without Embiid
headlines.summary: Portland beat Philadelphia 128–111. Deni Avdija scored 31 points with five threes, and the Blazers made 19 threes in total. Joel Embiid missed the game with an illness. The 76ers had a 14–4 record, and this was only their fourth loss of the season.

headlines.title: Reaves moves closer to a return for the Lakers
headlines.summary: Austin Reaves was a full participant at Lakers practice on Sunday after missing four straight games with a left heel bruise. The Lakers did no live-action drills, and Reaves has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Jazz. Coach JJ Redick said Reaves is improving by the day, and the team is working on equipment changes for him. Luka Doncic is averaging a league-leading 37.2 points per game for Los Angeles, which is 14–3.

headlines.title: Kings sign Gabe Vincent for depth
headlines.summary: Sacramento is finalising a deal with Gabe Vincent to fill its 15th roster spot, according to ESPN's Shams Charania. Vincent finished last season with Atlanta and has also played for Miami. The Kings have been looking for backup point guard depth since Ben Simmons tore his Achilles before the season, and they have rookie Darius Acuff Jr. at the position.

headlines.title: Sixers keep rolling in the East
headlines.summary: Philadelphia leads the East at 14–3 after five straight wins. It came back from a 17-point deficit against Orlando on Wednesday in a shorthanded win, then survived a late Bucks surge on Saturday. The Sixers have upgraded Brown, Wade and Bona to probable for Monday's game against Portland.

headlines.title: Herro's 50 not enough as Sixers hang on
headlines.summary: Tyler Herro scored a career-high 50 points, including a contested fadeaway three at the end of regulation that would have tied the game. An official review ruled he released it after the buzzer, so Philadelphia won 132–129. Joel Embiid had 26 points, 17 rebounds and nine assists, and LeBron James scored 13 of his 21 points in the fourth quarter. The Sixers nearly blew a 10-point late lead, and Jaylen Brown and Dean Wade were out with left hamstring injuries. The win moved them to 14-3, tied for the NBA's best record and their best 17-game start since 2000–01, according to ESPN.

headlines.title: Commanders stun Bengals on a last-drive field goal
headlines.summary: Cincinnati kicked a go-ahead field goal with 46 seconds left, but Jayden Daniels answered with two long throws to rookie Antonio Williams. The second, a 42-yard catch-and-run, set up Drew Stevens' 26-yard field goal as time expired. Williams finished with nine catches for 122 yards, and Daniels threw for 283 yards. Joe Burrow threw for 300 yards and two touchdowns for Cincinnati, but the Washington defence kept the Bengals to checkdowns for most of the night. The win was Washington's second in a row, and it moves them to 4-5-1.

headlines.title: Bills are looking at the AFC one seed
headlines.summary: Buffalo is 9–1 after six straight wins, and it has a four-game lead in the AFC East. The Jaguars and Bengals both lost to NFC East teams this week, which opens a path for the Bills to clinch the AFC's top seed. The piece points out that the Bills still have to win the rest of their AFC games to get the overall and conference records they need. Buffalo has never held the one seed during Josh Allen's career.

headlines.title: Giants move up the NFC after upset of Jaguars
headlines.summary: The Giants beat the Jaguars in an upset, and the win has changed how people view them. New York is 6–3–1 and third in the NFC playoff picture. Yahoo's power rankings now treat the Giants as a real contender, and their chances of winning the NFC East have improved.

headlines.title: Cowboys' offence puts up 51 on the Titans
headlines.summary: Dallas beat Tennessee 51–30 and scored on all but one possession. Dak Prescott completed 28 of 33 passes for 325 yards and four touchdowns, with no interceptions, and added a rushing score. CeeDee Lamb caught 11 of 12 targets for 132 yards and a touchdown. The Titans have now lost four straight and are 1–9. The win lifts the Cowboys to 5–6.

headlines.title: AFC playoff picture shuffles after Week 11
headlines.summary: The Broncos are back to the No. 2 seed after beating the Raiders, and they have retaken the AFC West lead on a tiebreaker. The Chiefs dropped to No. 5 despite a 34–7 win over the Cardinals. The Bengals remain No. 3 and play Monday night. The Jaguars are No. 4 and still hold a large lead in the AFC South, even after losing to the Giants. The Browns, who had a bye, moved up to No. 6, and the Steelers fell to No. 7 after losing to the Eagles.

headlines.title: Titans hold the top pick for the 2027 draft for now
headlines.summary: The Titans lost 51–30 to Dallas but remain on track for the first pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. The Chargers and Dolphins also fell to 1–9 in Week 11. The Chargers lost 27–24 to the Jets, and the Dolphins lost 26–9 to the Bills.

headlines.title: Saints' season slides to 3–7
headlines.summary: New Orleans lost 21–13 to the Bears on Sunday, its second straight defeat. Captain Justin Reid was released last week at his own request, and the Saints fired run game coordinator T.J. Paganetti. There have been offensive line injuries and kicking problems. Quarterback Tyler Shough still says the team is good and has been in every game except the Week 4 loss to Atlanta.

headlines.title: Nacua out four to five months after knee surgery
headlines.summary: Sources told ESPN that Puka Nacua's MCL recovery is four to five months, which rules him out of the playoffs. The surgery was on Tuesday, and his knee was clean apart from the MCL. In seven games he had 70 catches for 715 yards and four touchdowns. He is also serving a three-game suspension on injured reserve, and the NFL didn't know he'd had surgery when it imposed it. Coach Sean McVay said a postseason return hasn't been considered.
